callout.title: Four pre-flight verification checks before the first paid filing
callout.body: Each check requires retained evidence and an accountable owner. A verbal assurance does not repair a missing agreement, deadline, or cash reconciliation.
items: Authority and privacy: executed provider representation terms, HIPAA BAA, subcontractor obligations, and tested least-privilege access cover every recipient of protected records.
Eligibility and timing: documented plan funding, service eligibility, state-law analysis, negotiation evidence, batching rationale, and independently verified filing dates support the dispute.
Liquidity and fee exposure: at least 50% of launch capital remains allocated to reserve, with funded deposit responsibilities and a positive stressed thirteen-week cash forecast.
Economics and evidence: a sample invoice reproduces incremental collected cash after allocated costs, while excluded evidence and unpaid determinations remain outside the recovery fee calculation.

sop_steps.action: Match actual provider receipts to the baseline and cost-adjusted contingency.
sop_steps.detail: Release the first invoice only after bank evidence supports the waterfall; expand volume using observed collection lag and labor minutes rather than favorable-award percentages.

chapters.pull_quote: Protect the clock, preserve the reserve, and invoice the collected uplift rather than the promise of an award.
action_checklist: Allocate $5,500 of a $10,000 launch or $25,000 of a $45,000 launch to protected working capital, then reconcile every remaining budget line.

Validate ERA parsing, plan-funding evidence, business-day deadlines, batching criteria, and ninety-day suspension logic against documented test cases.

chapters.executive_summary: Candidate #45, Rank #09 of 49, scores 94/100, but its small-team advantage disappears when eligibility defects, missed deadlines, and uncollected awards masquerade as production. This chapter organizes 12 mapped plays: eleven chapter-local recovery controls and the supplied level-funded benefits advisory adjacency. The canonical annual owner-profit cases are $33,000 Conservative, $217,150 Base, and $504,000 Scaled, supported by earned operator revenue of $110,000, $505,000, and $900,000. None includes baseline provider collections or unpaid awards. Use claim-level jurisdiction evidence, business-day clocks, fee-adjusted incremental cash, and documented reversal reserves to protect those economics. The question's 80% framing is not an observed failure statistic; the actionable subject is preventable capital loss.

sections.heading: 1. Reject jurisdiction defects before they become paid filings
paragraphs: The first fatal trap is treating every out-of-network short payment as federal IDR inventory. Coverage, service category, date, location, and the applicable payment-setting law determine the route; a payer logo does not. The second is equating ERISA status with automatic federal eligibility. Distinguish self-funded plans, fully insured coverage, applicable specified state law, and relevant state opt-in arrangements before assigning a filing queue. Capture the plan sponsor, administrator, funding evidence, service location, emergency status, facility network status, and any notice-and-consent documentation. Ground-ambulance claims generally sit outside these federal surprise-billing protections; air-ambulance disputes require their own analysis. A denial involving coverage or medical necessity may require an appeal rather than a payment-amount arbitration. Chapter-local play P01, jurisdiction proof, buys a second check before money leaves the account. If screening costs $20 per claim, screening 100 claims costs $2,000; preventing four defective filings with $750 of otherwise stranded fees and work avoids $3,000, leaving $1,000 of illustrative protection. The fallback is a documented state-law, contractual, or benefit-appeal route, never relabeling the claim to fit federal eligibility. Retain the source document behind every routing decision, including the effective date of the rule used.

The third trap is confusing the initial filing clock with the negotiation period. Ordinarily, open negotiation must be initiated within 30 business days after receipt of the initial payment or denial; the negotiation period itself lasts 30 business days, followed by a four-business-day federal IDR initiation window. Extensions and special circumstances require evidence, not a salesperson's promise. Chapter-local play P02, deadline provenance, stores the actual receipt event, negotiation delivery evidence, applicable holiday calendar, and calculated last permissible action. Set an internal initiation target two business days before the legal deadline and require a second reviewer whenever receipt dates disagree. An 835 transaction date is not automatically proof of when the provider received the payment or denial. Chapter-local play P03, authority validation, links each submission to the correct provider entity, NPI, tax identifier, and written representative authority. A shared spreadsheet that silently changes time zones can destroy an otherwise strong recovery. For 50 cases carrying $400 of expected operator contribution each, one missed batch risks $20,000; a $300 monthly calendar and review budget is inexpensive by comparison. When authority or timing remains unresolved, stop new submissions for that cohort and preserve the available correction or extension evidence.

The fourth trap is batching for convenience instead of legal eligibility. Chapter-local play P04, batch integrity, groups only disputes satisfying the applicable version of the batching requirements and preserves a manifest of every included item. Do not assume that a shared payer brand, specialty, or spreadsheet tab establishes the required party and service relationships. Validate the service window, provider identity, plan or issuer identity, and permitted item or service grouping against current controlling rules and CMS instructions. Chapter-local play P05, cooling-period separation, tracks the 90-calendar-day restriction after a determination for the relevant parties and same or similar items or services. Preserve affected claims for the applicable post-period initiation pathway; the rule provides a subsequent 30-business-day window for qualifying suspended disputes, not permission to ignore their records. Litigation and implementation changes make a versioned rule register essential. At an illustrative $600 entity-fee exposure per defective filing, five bad submissions consume $3,000 before staff time. The fallback is a smaller eligible batch or individual filing supported by the effective rules, not a manipulated code. Keep the original coding intact and send genuine coding errors back through the provider's authorized correction process.

sections.heading: 2. Reconcile earned fees to collected cash, not arbitration headlines
paragraphs: The fifth trap is booking the selected offer as collected revenue. Chapter-local play P06, baseline reconciliation, distinguishes the payer's disclosed QPA from its actual initial allowed amount and payment. They are not interchangeable fields. Define the baseline using the signed engagement and claim-level remittance record, then identify only additional payer cash actually received and matched to that claim. Patient cost-sharing, the original provider collection, and outstanding awards do not become operator revenue. Chapter-local play P07, fee-adjusted settlement, applies the contracted contingency percentage only after unrecovered administrative fees, entity fees, and agreed casework costs. Consider an illustrative $12,000 initial payer payment followed by $8,000 of additional deposited recovery. Assume a $125 administrative charge, a $600 entity deposit subsequently refunded, and $600 of casework costs. These are modeling inputs, not representations of current published charges. After the refund clears, the distributable recovery base is $8,000 minus $125 minus $600, or $7,275. A 30% contingency earns $2,182.50. Before that refund clears, retain the $600 reserve and limit the provisional fee base to $6,675. The remaining $600 is neither earned fee revenue nor spendable working capital merely because the operator expects to prevail.

The sixth trap is assuming all unsuccessful or dismissed cases have identical refund treatment. Budget the CMS administrative fee as nonrefundable and reserve the certified entity fee through actual reconciliation. The prevailing party's entity-fee refund follows the applicable process; losing cases expose that fee to forfeiture. For ineligibility dismissals, conservatively reserve the full charge unless the effective instructions and entity policy establish a return, and recognize recovery only when received. Chapter-local play P08, reversal reserve, also covers payer recoupments, duplicate payments, corrected remittances, and provider refunds. Never distribute against an unmatched EFT. In the example, a failed claim with no incremental recovery can strand $125 plus $600 plus $600, or $1,325. The contract must identify who bears that loss; concealing it inside the next provider's settlement creates both trust and accounting problems. At cohort level, 100 initiated disputes with 75 favorable determinations but only 60 paid recoveries of $2,000 generate $120,000 of incremental cash, not $150,000. If unrecovered fees total $20,000 and casework costs total $10,000, the contingency base is $90,000 and a 30% operator share is $27,000. The other fifteen favorable outcomes remain collection work, not another $9,000 of earned fees.

The seventh trap is double counting revenue while hiding the expense burden. Formula v2.0 fixes Conservative operator revenue at $110,000, expenses at $77,000, and owner net profit at $33,000, a 30% margin with 1 FT + 2 C. Base uses $505,000, $287,850, and $217,150, respectively, a 43.0% margin with 1 FT + 2 C. Scaled uses $900,000, $396,000, and $504,000, a 56% margin with 2 FT + 3 C. These revenues are earned contingency shares, not underlying provider collections or award face values. The model treats the operator's retained earned share as revenue; document the ASC 606 principal-versus-agent assessment rather than automatically grossing up money handled for providers. Expenses already deducted in the provider settlement must not be deducted again as unreimbursed operator costs. Conversely, costs the operator actually absorbs remain expenses. At an illustrative uniform 30% contingency, the three revenue targets require approximately $366,667, $1,683,333, and $3,000,000 of fee-adjusted collected recovery bases. Those bases are operating requirements, not additional revenue scenarios. A monthly close should bridge bank deposits, provider liabilities, refunds, retained fees, overhead, and owner profit, with every unresolved difference assigned to a person and a dated resolution task.

sections.heading: 3. Detect operational decay before access restrictions or recoupments spread
paragraphs: The eighth trap is replacing evidence with a persuasive template. Chapter-local play P09, offer integrity, requires a sourced explanation of the proposed payment and a documented review of relevant permitted factors. QPA is an input, not a license to invent clinical acuity or a universal multiplier that wins every dispute. Licensed FAIR Health material can inform research where permitted, but identify the statistic, source rights, population, and relevance; an impermissible charge benchmark does not become usable because a vendor sold it. The federal framework excludes certain considerations, including usual and customary charges, billed charges, and public-payer reimbursement rates. Respect the effective rules and court decisions governing how permissible information is weighed. A clinician validates acuity statements against the actual encounter; the operator never changes medical documentation to improve the offer. For 40 briefs requiring 30 minutes of expert review at $120 per hour, quality assurance costs $2,400. Avoiding four $750 defective filings already offsets that amount. The fallback for weak evidence is a narrower supportable offer or negotiated settlement. Copying another provider's outcome, fabricating a comparator, or deleting unfavorable records can turn an ordinary collection dispute into contractual exposure, referral risk, and a loss of portal access.

The ninth trap is treating patient information as harmless sales material. Chapter-local play P10, access containment, begins with a HIPAA business associate agreement when the relationship requires one, approved subcontractor arrangements, role-based access, and audit retention. An 835 ERA parser should extract CARC and RARC signals into a controlled queue, not send raw patient records to a personal mailbox or an unapproved public AI service. Apply minimum-necessary practices where required and follow the applicable Security Rule safeguards for electronic protected health information. Portal accounts must identify authorized people; do not share credentials, rotate fictitious identities, or evade rate limits after access is restricted. Use supported interfaces and permitted automation, with retries bounded by documented service behavior. Suspend the affected integration on the first unexplained access denial or material authorization mismatch; preserve the event and contact the appropriate administrator. For a five-person operation, one shared login creates five indistinguishable sources of error, while named accounts make investigation and revocation practical. The fallback is a controlled manual workflow using authorized access, not an alternate account designed to bypass enforcement. Report suspected incidents through the established response process, assess notification duties, and prevent the same credentials from reaching unaffected provider workspaces.

The tenth trap is scaling intake while collection quality decays. Chapter-local play P11, cohort circuit breakers, measures eligibility dismissals, deadline misses, unpaid determinations, refund aging, and reversals by provider, payer, service category, and filing month. The thresholds here are internal triggers, not statutory tolerances. A single missed statutory deadline freezes new work in the affected queue until the clock defect is corrected. More than 2% eligibility dismissals across the latest 50 resolved filings triggers full re-screening; fewer than 50 observations require review of every dismissal rather than a reassuring percentage. Payment is generally due within 30 calendar days after determination under the federal framework; track the specific obligation and escalate overdue balances through documented payer contacts and appropriate complaint channels. If more than 20% of favorable determined dollars remain unpaid beyond 45 days, stop increasing that payer's exposure. If reversals exceed 3% of trailing 90-day incremental cash, recalculate the reserve before distributing more fees. These are conservative management choices, not evidence of industry averages. A $10,000 reserve funding $1,000 weekly net cash burn lasts ten weeks; favorable outcome statistics cannot extend that runway. The fallback is fewer paid filings, tighter evidence review, and active collections, not pressure on patients to fund the shortfall.

sop_steps.action: Stop additional paid submissions and discretionary distributions for the identified defect.

sections.heading: 4. Keep adjacent benefits revenue from contaminating the recovery engine
paragraphs: The eleventh trap is selling a benefits restructuring project as a guaranteed cure for disputed provider payments. The supplied mapped play, erisa_level_funded_transparent_pbm_bor_arbitrage, belongs to TRACK_1 and is the twelfth play in this chapter's map, alongside local controls P01 through P11. Use public Form 5500 Schedule A and Schedule C information, where filed and informative, to identify renewal timing and compensation-review opportunities. These filings have reporting limits and lags; they do not establish current claim jurisdiction, hidden misconduct, or permission to contact individual patients. Obtain employer authorization for a CAA 2021 service-provider compensation-disclosure review under ERISA section 408(b)(2)(B). A properly licensed advisory team may seek a broker-of-record appointment and disclose direct and indirect compensation. At $40 PEPM for 250 covered employees, the advisory fee is $10,000 monthly and $120,000 annually; at $65 PEPM it is $16,250 monthly and $195,000 annually. Define the billing population explicitly so employee and member counts cannot be interchanged. These are separate illustrative advisory receipts, not additions to the canonical recovery scenarios. If licensing, scope, or compensation transparency is incomplete, narrow the assignment to authorized disclosed work with qualified partners rather than collecting brokerage compensation through an unrelated IDR invoice.

The twelfth trap is assuming unbundling necessarily lowers employer cost. Compare the existing bundled arrangement with separately contracted TPA administration, stop-loss coverage, suitable captive participation, and a transparent pass-through PBM only after defining equivalent benefits and risk assumptions. Specify attachment points, lasers, exclusions, terminal liability, runout funding, collateral, and claim-payment timing. NADAC is a published acquisition-cost reference, not a complete pharmacy contract. An explicitly defined NADAC-based methodology needs the applicable publication date, dispensing fees, specialty-drug treatment, rebate ownership, audit rights, and a negotiated fallback for drugs without a usable NADAC value. For 250 employees, a quoted $12 PEPM administrative reduction equals $36,000 annually. If incremental stop-loss and collateral carrying costs total $45,000, the proposal is already $9,000 worse before adding advisory fees or transition work. Do not bury those costs in a different exhibit. The fallback is to retain or competitively rebid the existing structure, obtain explicit pricing fallbacks, and postpone implementation until the employer accepts the risk-adjusted economics. Keep employer advisory records separate from provider recovery records; neither relationship creates automatic authority to reuse the other's protected information or negotiate on behalf of an adverse party without a documented conflict assessment.

The thirteenth trap is financing an evidence-heavy recovery business with fee commitments that exceed its cash buffer. The canonical startup range is $10,000 to $45,000, monthly operating expense range is $1,800 to $10,500, and first-deal timing is one to four months. Those ranges are planning inputs, not complete annual cost bridges: case charges, reimbursable pass-throughs, staffing, and the owner's compensation treatment must still reconcile to the three canonical scenarios. At $10,500 monthly overhead, four months consumes $42,000 before incremental filing exposure, leaving only $3,000 from a $45,000 opening balance. Do not commit that remainder to a large payer cohort whose determinations have not converted into cash. Maintain a thirteen-week cash forecast separating provider money, earned operator fees, refundable deposits, nonrecoverable charges, and reversal reserves. Require a positive stress-case balance after assuming no new collections for the next eight weeks and funding already committed case costs. If that test fails, reduce intake, renegotiate authorized expense funding, or return incomplete files before incurring charges. The durable advantage is selective underwriting of collectible claims with defensible evidence, not the maximum number of portal submissions a small team can generate in a day.

chapters.subtitle: Mine NPPES, CMS Dispute Reports and Practice Transitions; Qualify ERISA Jurisdiction; Convert Protected Remittance Audits into Cash-Based Recovery Mandates
chapters.executive_summary: Candidate #45, No Surprises Act (IDR) Medical Arbitration & Out-of-Network Recovery, holds Rank #09 of 49 and a 94/100 Money-to-Manpower Score. This chapter maps 12 sourcing plays into one disciplined acquisition system: identify exposed physician groups, verify timely eligible claims, demonstrate recoverable economics, and secure narrow paid mandates. Public records establish account-level intent; authorized remittance audits establish actual opportunity. The first 3–10 wins mean signed, operationally accepted mandates within 1–4 months, not promised arbitration collections. Canonical annual owner profit is $33,000 Conservative, $217,150 Base, and $504,000 Scaled. Revenue consists only of earned contingency shares on incremental cash after specified deductions. Deadline discipline, jurisdiction screening, and payer cash reconciliation protect the spread better than indiscriminate filing volume.

sections.heading: 1. Mine account-level intent without confusing public signals with eligible claims
paragraphs: Start with independent emergency medicine, anesthesiology, radiology, pathology, and neonatology groups serving facilities where federal surprise-billing protections may apply. Build an account universe from the CMS National Plan and Provider Enumeration System downloadable files and NPI Registry API, then resolve organization names against practice websites and state business registries. An NPI taxonomy identifies a prospect category; it does not establish network status, coverage, standing, or a recoverable dispute. Store organization NPI, specialty, operating states, facility relationships, public business contact, source URL, and retrieval date. Treat the billing manager, revenue-cycle director, and practice administrator as separate buying roles rather than buying three copies of the same lead. Use CMS federal IDR public-use reports to prioritize broad service and payer patterns, never to infer a specific practice's unpaid award. A public hiring notice for an arbitration analyst, a new facility staffing contract, or a billing-vendor transition is a stronger conversation trigger than generic specialty membership. Screen each trigger manually before outreach. A practice that recently moved entirely in-network can look attractive in stale directories while having almost no new federal IDR inventory. Refresh high-priority accounts monthly and preserve historical source snapshots.

Implement public_record_api_intelligence as a modest, auditable collection pipeline, not an indiscriminate scrape. A scheduled Python urllib job can fetch permitted official feeds, while sqlite3 retains source hashes, timestamps, and deduplication keys. Use county civil dockets for public practice ownership disputes or billing-vendor litigation that indicates operational change; use probate registries only when a publicly documented practice succession creates a legitimate business contact. Unclaimed property ledgers can reveal a provider entity's stale payment address, but those assets are a separate recovery category and must never enter the IDR revenue forecast. Do not extract patient details from court exhibits or assume that public accessibility authorizes unrestricted reuse. A practical research budget is 100 accounts at 12 minutes each, or 20 hours; at an illustrative $40 hourly research cost, account discovery costs $800 before outreach. If access restrictions, unstable interfaces, or missing coverage undermine an API, switch to scheduled bulk FOIA/public-record exports, official data feeds, and low-frequency cached queues. Respect access terms and request only business-level fields. The fallback preserves research continuity, not filing timeliness: statutory clocks must come from authorized claim records, never delayed public-record responses.

The twelve plays below are a chapter-local sourcing map; only public_record_api_intelligence is a supplied cross-series identifier. Combine them into three queues: immediately contactable practice triggers, partner-introduced accounts, and inbound education requests. Every queue feeds the same qualification process. An HFMA chapter presentation can generate permission-based introductions, while an RBMA educational session may surface radiology groups with fragmented remittance workflows. A billing company is valuable because it can introduce several authorized clients, not because it can disclose every client's records. Require each provider's authorization and the appropriate HIPAA arrangements before receiving protected information. Do not offer percentage referral payments to clinicians or billing vendors without evaluating the actual federal and state restrictions; unpaid introductions avoid making referral compensation the acquisition thesis. At an illustrative 20 accounts per weekly research batch, four batches produce 80 distinct accounts, not 80 qualified mandates. Deduplicate across partner lists and events using organization identity rather than contact email. Measure qualified meetings per source and subsequent cash contribution per cohort. Retire a channel after two completed test cohorts if it produces meetings but no timely, eligible, economically workable inventory.

callout.title: Find the operational leak before pitching arbitration volume
callout.body: Experienced operators prospect for recoverable workflow failures and documented business changes, not merely large out-of-network balances.
items: Ask who reconciles initial payment receipt dates; an unowned date field often explains missed initiation windows.
Compare organization NPI and contracting entity before merging accounts; one staffing brand can contain several distinct billing groups.

Keep a separate ledger for unclaimed property and ordinary receivables leads so unrelated assets never inflate the federal IDR pipeline.

sections.heading: 2. Score eligibility, deadline runway and collectible contribution before accepting inventory
paragraphs: Qualification begins with a protected evidence package, not a spreadsheet of billed charges. Execute the service agreement, HIPAA Business Associate Agreement, and access instructions before handling protected health information; extend appropriate obligations to subcontractors. Request a limited recent sample containing the 835 remittance, underlying claim, service date, initial payment or denial receipt evidence, provider and facility identifiers, plan information, and prior negotiation correspondence. An 835 CARC/RARC classifier can identify adjustment patterns, but cannot conclusively determine federal jurisdiction or plan funding. A commercial payer logo does not distinguish its insured products from self-funded administrative-services business. Confirm coverage, applicable state law, service setting, network relationships, and the payment-determination method before calculating an opportunity. Some self-funded plans can opt into specified state arrangements; some services follow an applicable All-Payer Model Agreement. Exclude Medicare and Medicaid inventory from this commercial federal IDR sourcing model and route ordinary contractual disputes elsewhere. The federal mechanism is not a universal underpayment remedy. Record the basis for each eligibility decision and its reviewer. If a missing document could change the jurisdictional result, put the claim in a document-request queue rather than purchasing an arbitration filing on an assumption.

Build separate states for initial-payment receipt, open-negotiation initiation, negotiation completion, IDR initiation, entity selection, submissions, determination, and cash receipt. Under the federal framework, the open-negotiation notice generally must be initiated within 30 business days after receipt of the initial payment or denial; the negotiation period itself then runs for 30 business days. IDR initiation generally occurs during the four-business-day period beginning after negotiation ends. The four days are an initiation window, not permission to batch unrelated claims. Verify current CMS instructions, applicable extensions, litigation effects, and the rule version governing the particular dispute before scheduling action. Keep service dates distinct from receipt dates and retain proof of notice transmission. The 90-calendar-day restriction following a determination requires party and same-or-similar-service tracking, with the applicable later initiation window handled explicitly. Do not reduce it to a single universal payer/CPT timer. Batching requires its own current-rule eligibility check; a shared payer brand alone is insufficient. Assign an accountable human to each imminent deadline and an escalation backup. A nightly exception report should surface missing receipt evidence, disputed plan classification, expired clocks, and cooling-off conflicts before staff prepare an offer.

Use a 100-point account score only after mandatory eligibility checks pass: verified federal inventory earns 25 points, deadline runway 20, evidence completeness 20, collectible contribution 20, and administrator access 15. Seventy-five points qualifies a practice for a bounded pilot; no score rescues an ineligible claim. Define the contractual fee base as incremental cash collected above the actual initial payer payment, less non-refundable administrative fees, unrecovered entity fees, and agreed casework costs, floored at zero. QPA and initial allowed payment are distinct fields; never replace the actual baseline with an assumed QPA payment. Illustratively, $20,000 initially collected plus $10,000 subsequently collected creates $10,000 of incremental cash. Deduct $1,500 of administrative and unrecovered entity fees and $1,000 of casework costs: the distributable recovery is $7,500 and a 30% operator share is $2,250. These are aggregate sample costs, not published fee quotes. A $12,000 paper uplift with only $10,000 collected still supports only that $2,250 fee. Track entity-fee deposits separately: recognize a refund only when supported by actual disposition and receipt, and conservatively reserve losing or ineligible cases for full forfeiture unless the governing refund process establishes otherwise.

Confirm authority, protected data handling, current fees, loss reserves, and positive cash-based economics after every agreed deduction.

sections.heading: 3. Run a narrow outbound cadence that converts evidence into signed mandates
paragraphs: Run a five-touch, fifteen-business-day sequence around one documented business trigger. On day one, email the practice administrator a short observation and offer a twenty-line eligibility-and-deadline review, without requesting patient information by email. On day three, place a manual call to the published business number and ask who owns out-of-network recovery operations. On day six, send a permission-respecting professional-network message with a one-page explanation of the cash-based fee waterfall. On day ten, send a useful deadline-control worksheet; on day fifteen, close the loop and stop unless they invite further contact. Commercial email must use accurate routing and subject information, the required sender identification and postal address, a functioning opt-out, and timely suppression under 15 U.S.C. § 7704. Manual business outreach does not justify automated texts or prerecorded calls; evaluate the actual channel under 47 U.S.C. § 227 and applicable state rules before adding automation. Maintain one suppression list across email and partner campaigns. Never claim to represent CMS, a payer, or a certified IDR entity. The useful promise is a bounded assessment with documented exclusions, not an expected award or a guaranteed collection date.

Use explicit planning assumptions rather than fabricated industry conversion benchmarks. A starter cohort of 300 raw organization records might yield 180 verified eligible-profile accounts, a 60% research yield. If 30 engage in a relevant conversation, that is 16.7% of verified accounts; 15 discovery meetings represent 50% of conversations. Eight authorized sample reviews represent 53.3% of meetings, and three accepted mandates represent 37.5% of sample reviews, or 1% of raw records. These are test targets, not observed performance. Review source quality if the first 60 verified accounts produce fewer than six relevant conversations; review qualification or positioning if ten meetings produce fewer than two authorized samples. Do not compensate for poor conversion by filing marginal claims. If total acquisition spend is $4,500 and three mandates sign, acquisition cost is $1,500 per mandate. At an illustrative $2,250 earned fee per completed recovery cohort and $750 of additional operator delivery overhead, one collected cohort contributes $1,500 before acquisition expense, merely recovering that acquisition cost. Require evidence of repeat eligible inventory before paying for scale. Ten mandates at the same raw conversion would require 1,000 records and enough delivery capacity to service them without missing deadlines.

The discovery call should establish authority, inventory, process failure, and economics in that order. Ask who can authorize representation, how many recent potentially covered claims exist, which person owns receipt-date evidence, and whether another vendor already controls the same disputes. When the administrator says their billing company handles appeals, distinguish contractual appeals from timely federal open negotiation and IDR, then request a scoped coordination discussion rather than attacking the incumbent. When they cite a high published prevailing-offer percentage, explain that selection outcomes are not cash realization rates and request actual remittance history. When they demand a recovery guarantee, offer a fixed sample scope, documented eligibility findings, and cash-contingent compensation instead. When they resist data access, begin with aggregate counts and move to a minimum necessary protected sample only after contracting. The pilot mandate should identify the authorized provider entities, service-date range, payer scope, fee waterfall, expense funding, dispute authority, termination treatment, and reconciliation process. Require affirmative instructions about settlement authority; a contingency agreement alone should not imply unlimited discretion. Send the diagnostic findings within five business days of receiving complete records, while escalating any nearer statutory deadline immediately rather than waiting for the scheduled presentation.

sections.heading: 4. Land three mandates, prove the cash waterfall and scale only repeatable cohorts
paragraphs: Sequence the first four months around evidence delivery, not a premature filing target. During weeks one and two, configure the CRM, source register, suppression list, secure transfer environment, service agreement, and Business Associate Agreement. During weeks three and four, complete the first account cohort, run discovery calls, and accept only samples with adequate procedural runway. During weeks five through eight, deliver diagnostics, sign the first three bounded mandates, and initiate authorized negotiations on eligible inventory. During weeks nine through sixteen, expand toward ten mandates only if staffing and deadline coverage remain adequate. Count a sourcing win when the provider signs and the operating team accepts a viable scoped inventory; count a collected recovery separately. Fresh negotiations and subsequent arbitration can push cash beyond the acquisition window. Maintain distinct dashboard columns for signed mandates, accepted claims, negotiations initiated, disputes initiated, determinations, incremental collections, and earned fees. Existing disputes inherited from another vendor require explicit authority and procedural verification before any handoff. Never advertise a first-month collection timetable simply because one prospect has an old unpaid award. The acquisition plan must survive a slower cash cycle than the sales cycle.

Turn the diagnostic into a concise operating exhibit: eligible inventory, rejected inventory with reasons, next procedural dates, permitted evidence gaps, projected expenses, and a cash-waterfall example. Separate QPA-related information from prohibited pricing evidence. FAIR Health products may assist internal research where permitted, but a usual-and-customary charge benchmark must not be repackaged as permissible federal IDR valuation evidence. The federal framework excludes usual and customary charges, billed charges, and public payer reimbursement rates as determination factors. Use documented patient acuity, provider training and experience, facility characteristics, market share where relevant, and other permitted credible information without counting a factor twice through QPA and supplemental evidence. Assign submission drafting and eligibility review to different people when possible. After determination, track the statutory payment timetable, payment exceptions, and actual bank or remittance evidence; unpaid awards remain receivables rather than collected contingency revenue. Escalate delayed payment through the appropriate payer and CMS processes using retained records. Never transfer a protected patient balance to the patient to finance the dispute. Keep administrative fees, entity deposits, returned deposits, casework costs, baseline receipts, and incremental receipts in separate ledger fields so a provider can reproduce every invoice.

Reconcile scale to the canonical scorecard, not to physician collections. Conservative annual operator revenue is $110,000, with $77,000 of operator expenses and $33,000 owner profit at 30% margin using one full-time worker and two contractors. Base revenue is $505,000, expenses $287,850, and owner profit $217,150 at 43.0%, with the same team structure. Scaled revenue is $900,000, expenses $396,000, and owner profit $504,000 at 56%, using two full-time workers and three contractors. An illustrative $2,500 average earned fee requires 44, 202, and 360 collected recovery cohorts annually, respectively; cohort size is a modeling unit, not an authorized batching rule. Provider cash, paper awards, and refunded deposits are not substitutes for those fee totals. Costs already reimbursed or deducted in determining the contingency base must not be charged again as unreimbursed operator expenses. Use separate settlement and operator ledgers to prevent that duplication. Before hiring or buying another lead list, stress collection timing by an additional 60 days, reduce expected cash realization, and include losing or ineligible-case fee exposure. Pause expansion if the resulting working-capital requirement exceeds funded reserves, even when the mandate pipeline looks strong. High margin comes from disciplined selection and repeatable execution, not from celebrating uncollected awards.

sections.heading: 1. Build an admissible claim inventory before buying arbitration capacity
paragraphs: Begin with provider authority, a HIPAA Business Associate Agreement, and a read-only remittance feed rather than a spreadsheet of attractive charges. Obtain the original 837 claim, every associated 835 transaction, the explanation of benefits, relevant plan documents, service location, provider specialty, service date, and proof of initial payment or denial receipt. Parse CARC and RARC combinations into review queues, but never let an adjustment code establish federal jurisdiction by itself. A plan administrator's identity does not establish whether the coverage is self-funded, fully insured, or governed by an applicable state payment regime. For each claim, preserve the evidence supporting the applicable federal or state route and the person who verified it. Screen the covered service category, network relationships, emergency circumstances, facility status, and any relevant notice-and-consent facts. Federal IDR is not a universal appeal mechanism for every denied medical claim. Reject duplicates, contract disputes outside this pathway, and unsupported eligibility assertions before paying a filing-related fee. This first screen makes the difference between a recoverable underpayment and an expensive administrative rejection. Store the initial payer allowance and actual initial cash separately; neither field is automatically the QPA.

Build one immutable claim identity from the provider identifier, payer claim control number, service-line identity, and service date, retaining an alias map for corrected claims. The reference ledger uses a provider-scoped claim key and rejects a second enrollment even when a different cohort label is supplied. A corrected remittance updates the economic evidence through an adjustment event; it does not create another billable recovery. Attach a document manifest containing secure object references, hashes, source timestamps, and access restrictions. Keep clinical records outside the SQLite demonstration database, which is an accounting reference rather than an encrypted records repository. Use restricted storage such as an appropriately configured Amazon S3 deployment under the required service agreement, with separate access roles for intake, clinical review, and settlement. Export only the minimum evidence needed by the authorized recipient. Score priority using documented incremental recovery potential, remaining time, evidence completeness, expected unrecovered fees, and review minutes. A $4,000 potential increment with $800 of entity-fee exposure is a different assignment from a $600 increment with identical exposure. Where the record is incomplete, request the missing evidence or decline the case instead of manufacturing a favorable eligibility classification.

Maintain an externally reviewed business-day calendar and version every deadline calculation. The usual federal sequence starts with the window for initiating open negotiation within 30 business days after receipt of the initial payment or denial, followed by a 30-business-day negotiation period and a four-business-day IDR initiation window after that period ends. The four-day window concerns initiation, not a universal batching or entity-selection period. Preserve delivery evidence, recipient addresses, portal acknowledgments, and the calendar version used; an internal task completion flag is not evidence of service. Route extensions, portal interruptions, and disputed receipt dates to a named reviewer using the applicable current process rather than silently extending a deadline. For the 90-day cooling-off restriction, identify the initiating party, noninitiating party, and relevant same or similar items or services under the governing rule. Do not implement a simplistic payer-and-CPT lock that ignores party identity or applicable exceptions. Batching likewise requires a current eligibility test, not merely a shared spreadsheet tab. Plays one through seven below turn these requirements into assigned queues, artifacts, and measurable stop conditions before any arbitration package is released.

table.caption: Mapped Plays 1–7: Authorized Intake Through Federal IDR Initiation

Signed service authority, executed BAA, and hashed remittance source manifest
One hundred monthly leads enter one provider-scoped duplicate-control queue
Intake lead quarantines unmatched remittances before creating any recovery mandate
Play 2 — CARC and RARC recovery-priority classification
Original adjustment codes linked to clinical and payment evidence
Rank a $4,000 potential increment above a $600 equivalent-exposure increment
Reviewer rejects code-only eligibility conclusions and requests supporting source records
Play 3 — Federal versus state payment-route determination
Plan evidence, service category, location, and documented jurisdiction conclusion
Twenty of one hundred illustrative leads leave before entity-fee exposure
Jurisdiction reviewer routes state cases separately without federal filing charges
Play 4 — Initial payment and incremental-recovery baseline locking
Original payer allowance, QPA disclosure when available, and initial cash evidence
A $1,000 initial payment remains excluded from a later $4,000 increment
Settlement reviewer investigates corrected remittances before changing the locked baseline
Play 5 — Timely open-negotiation service and response tracking
Approved notice, receipt evidence, verified calendar, and negotiation correspondence
Track both the initiation window and the separate negotiation period
Deadline owner escalates missing delivery proof before treating negotiation as started
Play 6 — Eligible batching and cooling-off restriction management

Separate ineligible groupings before multiplying an illustrative $800 deposit exposure

Eighty eligible illustrative filings create individually tracked deadlines and deposits

callout.title: Four pre-flight checks before an external filing
callout.body: The reviewer signs the evidence manifest, not a generic completeness checkbox. No preparation token alone establishes that a notice or filing reached its recipient.
items: Verify provider authority, the BAA, federal eligibility evidence, and the original payment or denial receipt artifact.
Recalculate the negotiation and initiation deadlines against the reviewed calendar, including any documented applicable extension.
Verify current batching conditions and the party-specific cooling-off register; separate claims that cannot share the proposed submission.
Confirm the actual fee schedule, provider-funded reserve, permitted evidence package, and named owner of the portal acknowledgment.

sections.heading: 2. Install six reference modules with serialized ledger writes and explicit external handoffs
paragraphs: The six reference modules below can be concatenated, in order, into one Python 3.9 script and run against a local SQLite database. They use integer cents, foreign keys, unique source identities, immutable money events, and BEGIN IMMEDIATE transactions. Every read-modify-write operation acquires the write reservation before reading the state it will change. Concurrent local writers therefore cannot both claim the same preparation token or independently advance the same case version. A repeated request succeeds only when its recorded identity and contents match; conflicting reuse fails visibly. Keep the database on a local filesystem supported by SQLite locking, not a shared network drive, and give each process its own connection. A lock timeout means the transaction did not complete and must be retried with the same request identity. For multiple application hosts, port the transaction boundaries to PostgreSQL with row locks and identical uniqueness constraints. These guarantees cover the ledger, not a payer portal. No local database can atomically commit an independent website submission. The design therefore creates durable preparation work, permanently assigns it once claimed, and requires external receipt reconciliation before recording successful service.

The state machine deliberately distinguishes readiness from completed delivery. Verification records reviewed federal eligibility and a provider-controlled reserve; it does not represent operator custody of client money. Queueing open negotiation creates a preparation token, while confirmation requires a unique receipt and the delivered date. The reviewer supplies the verified negotiation end and IDR deadline after checking the actual service evidence. The same prepare, claim, and confirm sequence governs IDR initiation. A crashed worker does not release its claimed token automatically, because automatic reassignment could duplicate a submission that reached the portal just before the crash. Reconcile the external case status, then perform a separately audited recovery action if reassignment is necessary. The reference intentionally provides no blind resend function. Store only opaque evidence references in the ledger; authenticate users, authorize reviewer roles, encrypt storage and transport, and capture application audit records in the surrounding service. The executable core does not replace those deployment controls. Its purpose is narrower and testable: prevent duplicate local postings, conflicting transition acknowledgments, double allocation of one remittance line, and simultaneous ownership of the same external-action task.

Reconciliation works at the provider-cohort level because unsuccessful files still consume cash. Sum actual payer cash above each locked initial-payment baseline, deduct administrative charges, entity deposits less received refunds, and allocated casework costs, then apply the contracted contingency percentage to the positive remainder. Until an entity refund actually arrives, the deposit remains an economic deduction in this conservative cash model. The fee statement stores a ledger sequence cutoff and cumulative earned cents; later collections or reversals create a new statement adjustment rather than rewriting history. A separate receipt table records operator bank collections, allowing the reconciliation view to expose earned but unpaid service fees. Initial provider cash, provider reserves, entity refunds, and provider settlement proceeds are not operator revenue. The Base model uses a 20% retained contingency share only as its illustrative contract mechanic; the canonical $505,000 already represents operator service revenue, so applying that percentage again would understate revenue fivefold. Evaluate ASC 606 presentation against the actual service contract and principal-agent facts. Keep any fee reversals visible, and investigate negative client-fee balances instead of erasing them to make a dashboard look reconciled.

table.caption: Production Engineering / SQLite Ledger & Idempotent Workflow Reference Table — Six Copy-Pasteable Modules
rows: Module 1 — Create the database and immutable accounting structures

import json
import sqlite3
from contextlib import contextmanager
from datetime import date

db = sqlite3.connect(
    "idr_reference.sqlite3", timeout=30, isolation_level=None
)
db.row_factory = sqlite3.Row
db.execute("PRAGMA foreign_keys = ON")
db.execute("PRAGMA journal_mode = WAL")
db.execute("PRAGMA synchronous = FULL")
db.executescript("""
CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS cohort (
    cohort_id TEXT PRIMARY KEY,
    provider_id TEXT NOT NULL,
    period TEXT NOT NULL,
    fee_bps INTEGER NOT NULL CHECK(fee_bps BETWEEN 0 AND 10000),
    UNIQUE(provider_id, period),
    UNIQUE(cohort_id, provider_id)
);
CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS claim (
    case_id TEXT PRIMARY KEY,
    cohort_id TEXT NOT NULL,
    provider_id TEXT NOT NULL,
    claim_key TEXT NOT NULL,
    initial_cents INTEGER NOT NULL CHECK(initial_cents >= 0),
    intake_json TEXT NOT NULL,
    state TEXT NOT NULL DEFAULT 'intake'
        CHECK(state IN (
            'intake', 'verified', 'open_pending',
            'negotiating', 'idr_pending', 'filed'
        )),
    version INTEGER NOT NULL DEFAULT 0,
    verification_json TEXT,
    open_last TEXT,
    negotiation_end TEXT,
    idr_last TEXT,
    reserve_cents INTEGER NOT NULL DEFAULT 0
        CHECK(reserve_cents >= 0),
    FOREIGN KEY(cohort_id, provider_id)
        REFERENCES cohort(cohort_id, provider_id),
    UNIQUE(provider_id, claim_key)
);
CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS money_event (
    seq INTEGER PRIMARY KEY AUTOINCREMENT,
    event_id TEXT NOT NULL UNIQUE,
    case_id TEXT NOT NULL REFERENCES claim(case_id),
    kind TEXT NOT NULL CHECK(kind IN (
        'payer_cash', 'admin_fee', 'entity_deposit',
        'entity_refund', 'casework'
    )),
    cents INTEGER NOT NULL,
    source_system TEXT NOT NULL,
    source_ref TEXT NOT NULL,
    evidence_ref TEXT NOT NULL,
    UNIQUE(source_system, source_ref),
    CHECK(kind = 'payer_cash' OR cents >= 0)
);
CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS outbox (
    token TEXT PRIMARY KEY,
    case_id TEXT NOT NULL REFERENCES claim(case_id),
    action TEXT NOT NULL CHECK(action IN ('open', 'idr')),
    state TEXT NOT NULL DEFAULT 'prepared'
        CHECK(state IN ('prepared', 'claimed', 'confirmed')),
    actor TEXT,
    receipt TEXT UNIQUE,
    confirmation_json TEXT,
    UNIQUE(case_id, action)
);
CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS transition_log (
    seq INTEGER PRIMARY KEY AUTOINCREMENT,
    case_id TEXT NOT NULL REFERENCES claim(case_id),
    version INTEGER NOT NULL,
    state TEXT NOT NULL,
    evidence_ref TEXT NOT NULL,
    UNIQUE(case_id, version)
);
CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS fee_statement (
    token TEXT PRIMARY KEY,
    cohort_id TEXT NOT NULL REFERENCES cohort(cohort_id),
    cutoff INTEGER NOT NULL,
    earned_cents INTEGER NOT NULL,
    delta_cents INTEGER NOT NULL,
    UNIQUE(cohort_id, cutoff)
);
CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS fee_cash (
    token TEXT PRIMARY KEY,
    cohort_id TEXT NOT NULL REFERENCES cohort(cohort_id),
    cents INTEGER NOT NULL,
    bank_ref TEXT NOT NULL UNIQUE
);
CREATE TRIGGER IF NOT EXISTS money_no_update
BEFORE UPDATE ON money_event
BEGIN SELECT RAISE(ABORT, 'append correction evidence instead'); END;
CREATE TRIGGER IF NOT EXISTS money_no_delete
BEFORE DELETE ON money_event
BEGIN SELECT RAISE(ABORT, 'preserve original accounting evidence'); END;
CREATE TRIGGER IF NOT EXISTS statement_no_update
BEFORE UPDATE ON fee_statement
BEGIN SELECT RAISE(ABORT, 'issue a later statement adjustment'); END;
CREATE TRIGGER IF NOT EXISTS statement_no_delete
BEFORE DELETE ON fee_statement
BEGIN SELECT RAISE(ABORT, 'preserve original fee statement'); END;
""")

@contextmanager
def tx():
    db.execute("BEGIN IMMEDIATE")
    try:
        yield
        db.execute("COMMIT")
    except BaseException:
        db.execute("ROLLBACK")
        raise

def canonical(value):
    return json.dumps(value, sort_keys=True, separators=(",", ":"))

def iso(value):
    return date.fromisoformat(value).isoformat()

def require(condition, message):
    if not condition:
        raise ValueError(message)
All mutable accounting operations below serialize before reading dependent records; schema initialization runs before serving application traffic.
Use one connection per process, supported local disk locking, restricted database access, and independently tested encrypted backups.
Module 2 — Enroll authorized claims and score review priority

def enroll(cohort_id, provider_id, period, case_id, claim_key,
           initial_cents, fee_bps, evidence_ref,
           potential_increment_cents, expected_cost_cents,
           review_minutes):
    require(type(initial_cents) is int and initial_cents >= 0,
            "initial payment must be nonnegative integer cents")
    require(type(fee_bps) is int and 0 <= fee_bps <= 10000,
            "fee basis points must be an integer percentage")
    require(review_minutes > 0, "positive review time required")
    require(bool(evidence_ref), "source evidence required")
    payload = canonical({
        "cohort": cohort_id, "provider": provider_id,
        "period": period, "case": case_id, "claim": claim_key,
        "initial": initial_cents, "fee_bps": fee_bps,
        "evidence": evidence_ref,
        "potential": potential_increment_cents,
        "expected_cost": expected_cost_cents,
        "minutes": review_minutes,
    })
    with tx():
        old = db.execute(
            "SELECT intake_json FROM claim WHERE case_id = ?",
            (case_id,)
        ).fetchone()
        if old:
            require(old["intake_json"] == payload,
                    "case identity reused with conflicting intake")
        else:
            cohort = db.execute(
                "SELECT * FROM cohort WHERE cohort_id = ?",
                (cohort_id,)
            ).fetchone()
            if cohort:
                require(
                    (cohort["provider_id"], cohort["period"],
                     cohort["fee_bps"]) ==
                    (provider_id, period, fee_bps),
                    "cohort contract mismatch"
                )
            else:
                db.execute(
                    "INSERT INTO cohort VALUES (?, ?, ?, ?)",
                    (cohort_id, provider_id, period, fee_bps)
                )
            db.execute("""
                INSERT INTO claim (
                    case_id, cohort_id, provider_id, claim_key,
                    initial_cents, intake_json
                ) VALUES (?, ?, ?, ?, ?, ?)
            """, (case_id, cohort_id, provider_id, claim_key,
                  initial_cents, payload))
            db.execute("""
                INSERT INTO money_event (
                    event_id, case_id, kind, cents,
                    source_system, source_ref, evidence_ref
                ) VALUES (?, ?, 'payer_cash', ?, 'baseline', ?, ?)
            """, ("baseline/" + case_id, case_id, initial_cents,
                  case_id, evidence_ref))
            db.execute("""
                INSERT INTO transition_log (
                    case_id, version, state, evidence_ref
                ) VALUES (?, 0, 'intake', ?)
            """, (case_id, evidence_ref))
    return max(
        0, potential_increment_cents - expected_cost_cents
    ) // review_minutes
Enrollment and baseline posting commit together; the score ranks review effort without asserting legal eligibility or expected cash collection.
Replaying identical enrollment returns the same score; conflicting identity reuse or cross-cohort duplicate claims fail under unique constraints.
Module 3 — Verify evidence, reserve funds, and claim external preparation work

def verify(case_id, checks, open_last, reserve_cents):
    needed = {
        "authority", "baa", "federal_eligible",
        "receipt_verified", "calendar_verified",
        "batching_checked", "cooling_checked"
    }
    require(all(checks.get(key) is True for key in needed),
            "every reviewed eligibility check must pass")
    require(bool(checks.get("evidence_ref")),
            "verification evidence reference required")
    require(type(reserve_cents) is int and reserve_cents >= 0,
            "verified provider reserve must use integer cents")
    last = iso(open_last)
    payload = canonical({
        "checks": checks, "open_last": last,
        "reserve_cents": reserve_cents
    })
    with tx():
        row = db.execute(
            "SELECT * FROM claim WHERE case_id = ?", (case_id,)
        ).fetchone()
        require(row is not None, "case must exist")
        if row["verification_json"] is not None:
            require(row["verification_json"] == payload,
                    "verification replay conflicts with original")
            return
        require(row["state"] == "intake", "case already advanced")
        db.execute("""
            UPDATE claim SET state = 'verified',
                version = version + 1, verification_json = ?,
                open_last = ?, reserve_cents = ?
            WHERE case_id = ?
        """, (payload, last, reserve_cents, case_id))
        db.execute("""
            INSERT INTO transition_log (
                case_id, version, state, evidence_ref
            ) VALUES (?, ?, 'verified', ?)
        """, (case_id, row["version"] + 1, checks["evidence_ref"]))

def queue_action(case_id, action, required_reserve_cents=0):
    require(action in ("open", "idr"), "supported action required")
    require(type(required_reserve_cents) is int
            and required_reserve_cents >= 0,
            "required reserve must use nonnegative integer cents")
    token = action + "/" + case_id
    today = date.today().isoformat()
    with tx():
        old = db.execute(
            "SELECT token FROM outbox WHERE case_id = ? AND action = ?",
            (case_id, action)
        ).fetchone()
        if old:
            return old["token"]
        row = db.execute(
            "SELECT * FROM claim WHERE case_id = ?", (case_id,)
        ).fetchone()
        require(row is not None, "case must exist")
        if action == "open":
            require(row["state"] == "verified",
                    "open negotiation requires verified intake")
            require(today <= row["open_last"],
                    "open negotiation initiation window expired")
        else:
            require(row["state"] == "negotiating",
                    "IDR requires confirmed open negotiation")
            require(row["negotiation_end"] < today <= row["idr_last"],
                    "outside reviewed IDR initiation window")
            require(required_reserve_cents > 0,
                    "current filing reserve amount required")
            require(row["reserve_cents"] >= required_reserve_cents,
                    "provider reserve is insufficient")
        pending = "open_pending" if action == "open" else "idr_pending"
        db.execute("""
            INSERT INTO outbox (token, case_id, action)
            VALUES (?, ?, ?)
        """, (token, case_id, action))
        db.execute("""
            UPDATE claim SET state = ?, version = version + 1
            WHERE case_id = ?
        """, (pending, case_id))
        db.execute("""
            INSERT INTO transition_log (
                case_id, version, state, evidence_ref
            ) VALUES (?, ?, ?, ?)
        """, (case_id, row["version"] + 1, pending, token))
    return token

def claim_action(token, actor):
    require(bool(actor), "authenticated actor identifier required")
    with tx():
        row = db.execute(
            "SELECT * FROM outbox WHERE token = ?", (token,)
        ).fetchone()
        require(row is not None, "preparation token must exist")
        if row["state"] != "prepared":
            return False
        db.execute("""
            UPDATE outbox SET state = 'claimed', actor = ?
            WHERE token = ?
        """, (actor, token))
        return True
Provider-controlled reserves are verification facts rather than operator escrow balances; claimed work never automatically returns to the preparation queue.
One serialized claimant receives permission to act; repeated claims return false even for the same actor, preventing automatic duplicate delivery.
Module 4 — Confirm delivery and post source-identified cash events

def confirm_action(token, actor, receipt, delivered_on,
                   negotiation_end=None, idr_last=None):
    delivered = iso(delivered_on)
    require(bool(receipt), "external receipt identity required")
    payload = canonical({
        "actor": actor, "receipt": receipt,
        "delivered": delivered,
        "negotiation_end": negotiation_end, "idr_last": idr_last
    })
    with tx():
        task = db.execute(
            "SELECT * FROM outbox WHERE token = ?", (token,)
        ).fetchone()
        require(task is not None, "preparation token must exist")
        if task["state"] == "confirmed":
            require(task["confirmation_json"] == payload,
                    "confirmation replay conflicts with original")
            return
        require(task["state"] == "claimed" and task["actor"] == actor,
                "only the assigned actor may confirm delivery")
        row = db.execute(
            "SELECT * FROM claim WHERE case_id = ?",
            (task["case_id"],)
        ).fetchone()
        require(delivered <= date.today().isoformat(),
                "delivery cannot be recorded in the future")
        if task["action"] == "open":
            end = iso(negotiation_end)
            last = iso(idr_last)
            require(row["state"] == "open_pending",
                    "case is not awaiting open negotiation")
            require(delivered <= row["open_last"],
                    "delivered outside reviewed initiation window")
            require(delivered <= end < last,
                    "reviewed deadline ordering is inconsistent")
            target = "negotiating"
        else:
            require(row["state"] == "idr_pending",
                    "case is not awaiting IDR initiation")
            require(row["negotiation_end"] < delivered <= row["idr_last"],
                    "delivered outside reviewed IDR window")
            end, last, target = (
                row["negotiation_end"], row["idr_last"], "filed"
            )
        db.execute("""
            UPDATE outbox SET state = 'confirmed', receipt = ?,
                confirmation_json = ? WHERE token = ?
        """, (receipt, payload, token))
        db.execute("""
            UPDATE claim SET state = ?, version = version + 1,
                negotiation_end = ?, idr_last = ?
            WHERE case_id = ?
        """, (target, end, last, row["case_id"]))
        db.execute("""
            INSERT INTO transition_log (
                case_id, version, state, evidence_ref
            ) VALUES (?, ?, ?, ?)
        """, (row["case_id"], row["version"] + 1, target, receipt))

def post_money(event_id, case_id, kind, cents,
               source_system, source_ref, evidence_ref):
    allowed = {
        "payer_cash", "admin_fee", "entity_deposit",
        "entity_refund", "casework"
    }
    require(kind in allowed and type(cents) is int,
            "supported event and integer cents required")
    require(kind == "payer_cash" or cents >= 0,
            "cost and refund entries must be nonnegative")
    require(source_system != "baseline", "baseline namespace reserved")
    require(bool(source_ref) and bool(evidence_ref),
            "allocation identity and evidence required")
    values = (
        event_id, case_id, kind, cents,
        source_system, source_ref, evidence_ref
    )
    with tx():
        old = db.execute("""
            SELECT event_id, case_id, kind, cents,
                source_system, source_ref, evidence_ref
            FROM money_event WHERE event_id = ?
        """, (event_id,)).fetchone()
        if old:
            require(tuple(old) == values,
                    "money event replay conflicts with original")
            return
        if kind == "entity_refund":
            balance = db.execute("""
                SELECT COALESCE(SUM(
                    CASE kind
                        WHEN 'entity_deposit' THEN cents
                        WHEN 'entity_refund' THEN -cents
                        ELSE 0 END
                ), 0) FROM money_event WHERE case_id = ?
            """, (case_id,)).fetchone()[0]
            require(cents <= balance,
                    "entity refund exceeds recorded deposits")
        db.execute("""
            INSERT INTO money_event (
                event_id, case_id, kind, cents,
                source_system, source_ref, evidence_ref
            ) VALUES (?, ?, ?, ?, ?, ?, ?)
        """, values)

def post_fee_receipt(token, cohort_id, cents, bank_ref):
    require(type(cents) is int and cents != 0,
            "signed nonzero integer receipt cents required")
    require(bool(bank_ref), "unique operator bank evidence required")
    values = (token, cohort_id, cents, bank_ref)
    with tx():
        old = db.execute(
            "SELECT * FROM fee_cash WHERE token = ?", (token,)
        ).fetchone()
        if old:
            require(tuple(old) == values,
                    "fee receipt replay conflicts with original")
            return
        db.execute(
            "INSERT INTO fee_cash VALUES (?, ?, ?, ?)", values
        )
A bank source reference must identify an approved deposit-line allocation; signed payer adjustments preserve recoupments without rewriting initial cash.
External fee corrections require reviewed compensating accounting outside this narrow event vocabulary; no fabricated refund category is supplied.
Module 5 — Reconcile cohort fee bases and freeze auditable statements

db.executescript("""
CREATE VIEW IF NOT EXISTS case_cash AS
SELECT c.case_id, c.cohort_id,
    MAX(0, COALESCE(SUM(
        CASE WHEN e.kind = 'payer_cash' THEN e.cents ELSE 0 END
    ), 0) - c.initial_cents) AS incremental_cents,
    COALESCE(SUM(
        CASE e.kind
            WHEN 'admin_fee' THEN e.cents
            WHEN 'entity_deposit' THEN e.cents
            WHEN 'entity_refund' THEN -e.cents
            WHEN 'casework' THEN e.cents
            ELSE 0 END
    ), 0) AS deduction_cents
FROM claim c
LEFT JOIN money_event e ON e.case_id = c.case_id
GROUP BY c.case_id, c.cohort_id, c.initial_cents;

CREATE VIEW IF NOT EXISTS cohort_basis AS
SELECT h.cohort_id, h.fee_bps,
    COALESCE(SUM(c.incremental_cents), 0) AS incremental_cents,
    COALESCE(SUM(c.deduction_cents), 0) AS deduction_cents,
    MAX(0, COALESCE(SUM(
        c.incremental_cents - c.deduction_cents
    ), 0)) AS eligible_cents
FROM cohort h
LEFT JOIN case_cash c ON c.cohort_id = h.cohort_id
GROUP BY h.cohort_id, h.fee_bps;

CREATE VIEW IF NOT EXISTS cohort_reconciliation AS
SELECT b.*,
    CAST((b.eligible_cents * b.fee_bps + 5000) / 10000
         AS INTEGER) AS earned_fee_cents,
    COALESCE((
        SELECT SUM(f.cents) FROM fee_cash f
        WHERE f.cohort_id = b.cohort_id
    ), 0) AS received_fee_cents,
    CAST((b.eligible_cents * b.fee_bps + 5000) / 10000
         AS INTEGER) -
    COALESCE((
        SELECT SUM(f.cents) FROM fee_cash f
        WHERE f.cohort_id = b.cohort_id
    ), 0) AS fee_receivable_cents
FROM cohort_basis b;
""")

def freeze_statement(token, cohort_id):
    with tx():
        old = db.execute(
            "SELECT * FROM fee_statement WHERE token = ?", (token,)
        ).fetchone()
        if old:
            require(old["cohort_id"] == cohort_id,
                    "statement token reused for another cohort")
            return dict(old)
        cutoff = db.execute("""
            SELECT COALESCE(MAX(e.seq), 0)
            FROM money_event e
            JOIN claim c ON c.case_id = e.case_id
            WHERE c.cohort_id = ?
        """, (cohort_id,)).fetchone()[0]
        same = db.execute("""
            SELECT * FROM fee_statement
            WHERE cohort_id = ? AND cutoff = ?
        """, (cohort_id, cutoff)).fetchone()
        if same:
            return dict(same)
        row = db.execute("""
            SELECT earned_fee_cents FROM cohort_reconciliation
            WHERE cohort_id = ?
        """, (cohort_id,)).fetchone()
        require(row is not None, "cohort must exist")
        previous = db.execute("""
            SELECT earned_cents FROM fee_statement
            WHERE cohort_id = ? ORDER BY cutoff DESC LIMIT 1
        """, (cohort_id,)).fetchone()
        prior = previous["earned_cents"] if previous else 0
        earned = row["earned_fee_cents"]
        db.execute(
            "INSERT INTO fee_statement VALUES (?, ?, ?, ?, ?)",
            (token, cohort_id, cutoff, earned, earned - prior)
        )
        return dict(db.execute(
            "SELECT * FROM fee_statement WHERE token = ?", (token,)
        ).fetchone())

def qa_checks():
    require(db.execute("PRAGMA integrity_check").fetchone()[0] == "ok",
            "SQLite structural integrity check failed")
    require(not db.execute("PRAGMA foreign_key_check").fetchall(),
            "foreign key inconsistency detected")
    require(not db.execute("""
        SELECT c.case_id
        FROM claim c LEFT JOIN money_event e
          ON e.case_id = c.case_id AND e.source_system = 'baseline'
        GROUP BY c.case_id, c.initial_cents
        HAVING COUNT(e.seq) != 1
            OR COALESCE(SUM(e.cents), 0) != c.initial_cents
    """).fetchall(), "initial cash baseline does not reconcile")
    require(not db.execute("""
        SELECT case_id FROM money_event
        GROUP BY case_id
        HAVING SUM(CASE kind
            WHEN 'entity_deposit' THEN cents
            WHEN 'entity_refund' THEN -cents ELSE 0 END) < 0
    """).fetchall(), "entity refunds exceed recorded deposits")
    require(not db.execute("""
        SELECT token FROM outbox
        WHERE state = 'confirmed'
          AND (receipt IS NULL OR confirmation_json IS NULL)
    """).fetchall(), "confirmed delivery lacks receipt evidence")
    require(not db.execute("""
        SELECT c.case_id FROM claim c
        LEFT JOIN transition_log t
          ON t.case_id = c.case_id AND t.version = c.version
        WHERE t.seq IS NULL OR t.state != c.state
    """).fetchall(), "case state does not match transition evidence")
    warnings = db.execute("""
        SELECT cohort_id, fee_receivable_cents
        FROM cohort_reconciliation
        WHERE fee_receivable_cents != 0
    """).fetchall()
    return {
        "structural_checks": "passed",
        "fee_collection_exceptions": [dict(row) for row in warnings],
    }

sections.heading: 3. Run negotiation, evidence, awards, and cash recovery as separate queues
paragraphs: Assign negotiation and arbitration preparation to different work queues, even when one full-time operator owns both. Negotiation should articulate the specific payment disagreement, identify the relevant service lines, and preserve any binding settlement terms with payment instructions. For IDR, prepare the required offer and permitted supporting evidence under the current governing standards and submission schedule. Baseball arbitration selects an offer; it does not automatically award the operator's spreadsheet target. The QPA is a required consideration, but the brief must also address other applicable permissible information without presenting prohibited material. Use specialty training, patient acuity, complexity, facility teaching status where relevant, and documented good-faith contracting efforts only as supported and applicable. FAIR Health subscriptions can support internal research, but usual-and-customary charge evidence does not become permissible merely because it came from a named vendor. Do not base the determination request on prohibited billed charges, usual-and-customary charges, or public payer reimbursement rates. Have a qualified reviewer verify the evidence against current regulations and controlling decisions, especially where rule text and implementation guidance have changed. Preserve both submitted offers, the final determination, and the exact service-line scope.

Treat a favorable determination as an account to collect, not cash in the owner-profit column. Record the award amount, initial payment offset, applicable payment deadline, entity-fee refund status, and payer remittance instructions in a separate award register. The federal framework generally requires the resulting payment within 30 calendar days after the determination; review the case-specific obligation and any valid adjustment before escalation. Match each later 835 line to bank evidence and allocate partial payments without repeating the initial allowance deduction. If an award establishes a $5,000 total payment and $1,000 already arrived, a later $4,000 deposit is the increment, not another $5,000 recovery. A $2,000 partial deposit supports only $2,000 of incremental cash at that point. Track payer recoupments as signed events and recalculate the cumulative fee entitlement. Escalate overdue payment through the applicable documented payer and agency channels; do not rebill protected patients to replace the missing award cash. Provider-funded deposits stay outside operator working capital, and entity refunds must be matched to actual receipts. The owner dashboard should show filed cases, favorable determinations, paid determinations, incremental cash, earned fees, and collected operator fees as distinct measures.

The twelfth mapped play, wotc_hourly_payroll_tax_credit_contingency_engine, is a process analogue and a separate service line, not another medical recovery fee. For employer-authorized WOTC work, verify statutory authorization for the relevant hiring period, qualifying group evidence, certification procedure, and submission timing before promising a credit workflow. Form 8850 generally must reach the designated state workforce agency within 28 days after work begins, subject to applicable relief. An illustrative eligible worker with 400 qualifying hours and $6,000 of qualifying first-year wages could support a $2,400 credit under the general 40% calculation; 25 such workers imply $60,000 of employer credits, not operator revenue. A hypothetical permitted 10% outcome-linked fee would produce $6,000 only under a valid engagement and professional-fee analysis. Separately substantiate Section 41 qualified research expenses, business components, experimentation, wage allocation, and Section 280C coordination; never recycle WOTC screening into an R&D claim. Review applicable contingent-fee restrictions, including 31 CFR § 10.27 where relevant, with the responsible tax professional. Exclude unsupported claims and use fixed-fee payroll or research-documentation services under independent tax review when outcome-linked pricing is unavailable. None of these employer credits or fees enters the medical Base-case ledger.
