sections.heading: 4. Walk a mature 90-day book without pretending a startup collects immediately
paragraphs: The Worked 90-Day Cohort Walk is a mature-book illustration, not a claim that every new IDR file converts within ninety days. Each month brings 100 authorized leads; twenty scrub out before federal filing, leaving eighty eligible files. For the mature cohorts collected during this window, sixty-five files receive favorable determinations, ten lose, and five dismissals retain the assumed paid entity fees. Sixty favorable files actually pay a $4,000 increment during the modeled collection period, producing $240,000 of incremental provider cash. Five favorable files remain unpaid, representing $20,000 of prospective increments excluded from this period's revenue. Later receipts enter a later ledger cutoff and cannot be counted twice. Fees are explicit modeling assumptions, not representations of current CMS or entity schedules: eighty $100 administrative charges equal $8,000; eighty $800 entity deposits equal $64,000; sixty-five received $800 refunds equal $52,000. Unrecovered fees therefore equal $20,000. Verify actual administrative charges, entity schedules, refund eligibility, and dismissal terms before funding a real cohort. The five dismissed cases illustrate fee-retention exposure, rather than asserting that every dismissal has an identical refund outcome.

Allocate $9,583.35 of provider-borne casework to each of the first two settling cohorts and $9,583.30 to the third. Across the quarter, $720,000 of incremental cash minus $60,000 of unrecovered fees and $28,750 of casework leaves $631,250 of fee-eligible contribution. A 20% contingency produces exactly $126,250 of operator service revenue, with monthly fees of $42,083.33, $42,083.33, and $42,083.34. The provider separately bears the identified cohort expenses; they are not charged again inside operator overhead. Operator overhead is $23,987.50 monthly, or $71,962.50 quarterly, including modeled owner-team labor, contractor capacity, infrastructure, insurance, and business administration. For operating planning, that monthly total can be decomposed into $16,000 of labor and contractor expense plus $7,987.50 of other overhead. The latter fits the stated $1,800–$10,500 operating-overhead range; that range cannot substitute for the scorecard's all-in expense total. Quarterly owner profit is $54,287.50. Repeating this mature quarter four times yields $505,000 revenue, $287,850 expenses, and $217,150 profit, exactly 43.0%. Those are operator figures; provider settlement value and initial collections remain outside recognized revenue.

Month 1 collections come from pre-window cohort P1, Month 2 from P2, and Month 3 from P3; each entered early enough to complete its actual negotiation, determination, and collection sequence. New cohorts A, B, and C are tracked independently and contribute no assumed cash within this walk. Their eventual timing depends on negotiated settlements, proceedings, refunds, and payer behavior, not a fixed ninety-day promise. Provider-controlled reserves fund their case expenses, so those reserves do not improve operator cumulative cash. Assuming the mature cohorts' operator invoices are paid in the same month, cumulative operating cash reaches $18,095.83, $36,191.66, and $54,287.50 after monthly overhead. A cold start with identical staffing but no pre-window cohorts instead consumes $71,962.50 before setup costs if no operator fees arrive during the quarter. That exceeds the stated $10,000–$45,000 startup capital range and requires staged staffing, earlier documented negotiated collections, or additional runway. Time to first deal of one to four months is not time to unrestricted owner cash. Stress-test slower refunds, fewer paid favorable outcomes, and provider invoice delays before adding the second full-time seat; capacity expansion should follow reconciled throughput rather than the volume of favorable decision notices.

chapters.executive_summary: Candidate #45, Rank #09 of 49, scores 94/100 by turning documented out-of-network underpayments into a tightly controlled recovery workflow. This chapter connects 18 named resources to 12 mapped plays spanning provider discovery, jurisdiction screening, remittance normalization, deadline control, evidence assembly, and collected-cash reconciliation. Public records identify opportunities; authorized claim records establish eligibility; bank-matched receipts establish earned contingency revenue. Formula v2.0 fixes annual owner profit at $33,000 Conservative, $217,150 Base, and $504,000 Scaled, without counting baseline provider collections. The operating edge is a versioned evidence chain, not indiscriminate scraping: every source needs an access method, freshness rule, fallback, and accountable owner before its output influences a filing.

sections.heading: 1. Establish authoritative identities before enriching an opportunity
paragraphs: Start with an identity ledger, not a prospect spreadsheet. Give each provider organization, rendering clinician, payer legal entity, employer plan, and disputed service a separate internal identifier. NPPES supplies an NPI and published taxonomy; it does not establish network status, licensure, ownership, or federal IDR eligibility. Join an organization NPI to the signed engagement, authorized billing records, and relevant practice locations before attaching claims. Use CMS Care Compare to corroborate publicly reported affiliations, then verify current practice relationships directly. An apparent hospital affiliation is neither proof of employment nor proof that a particular encounter qualifies under the No Surprises Act. Store the source URL, retrieval time, effective period, and original artifact hash beside every asserted attribute. Keep contradictory observations rather than overwriting them. A directory address changed yesterday cannot retroactively establish the service location six months earlier. The first three chapter-local mapped plays are Provider Identity Resolution, Practice Affiliation Verification, and Federal-versus-State Routing. At 100 prospective practices and six minutes per identity check, initial screening consumes ten hours; resolving only twenty ambiguous matches at fifteen minutes each adds five hours. That bounded queue beats letting every ambiguous record consume a full arbitration analyst review.

Jurisdiction is a document question, not a payer-logo classifier. DOL Form 5500 records can corroborate an employer plan's existence and reported arrangements, but filing exemptions, reporting lag, and sponsor subsidiaries prevent a reliable one-field determination of funding status. Obtain the applicable plan documents, coverage details, initial remittance, service location, and evidence concerning any state election that matters to the encounter. Separate ERISA status from self-funding; neither label alone resolves every federal-versus-state payment issue. Test whether a specified state law or applicable All-Payer Model Agreement determines the payment amount before routing to federal IDR under 42 U.S.C. § 300gg-111. Medicare, Medicaid, and other excluded coverage must leave this commercial workflow. Record why the service category and circumstances meet the relevant federal protections, including emergency care or covered nonemergency services at participating facilities. For thirty uncertain claims, a twelve-minute document check costs six analyst hours; compare that with thirty avoidable filing expenditures and dismissed cases. The fallback is a missing-evidence queue with a named requester and deadline, not an automated federal filing based on an insurance card. State insurance department materials supplement, but do not replace, encounter-specific plan evidence.

Use CMS IDR public-use releases to understand the market's case mix, reporting periods, and operational congestion. They are aggregate observations, not a provider prospect list, a current case-status API, or a forecast that your offers will be collected. Preserve each release with its methodology because submissions, disputes, determinations, and payment outcomes have different denominators. A reported prevailing offer share cannot supply a collection probability without separate receipt evidence. The directory in this chapter contains eighteen named resources across three matrices; the fourth matrix contains operating tests rather than additional directory entries. Cost tiers distinguish free public access, included customer access, and negotiated licenses, because commercial endpoints rarely have universal pricing. Refresh cadence likewise separates a source's publication schedule from the desk's polling schedule. Do not manufacture a latency commitment where the publisher provides none. Maintain an acquisition manifest containing retrieval timestamps, response status, content hashes, parser version, and row counts. A public download that silently changes columns should fail into quarantine instead of rewriting the identity ledger. For six public sources checked weekly, twenty minutes of review per source budgets two hours; measure whether detected changes actually affect routing before increasing that frequency.

sections.heading: 2. Normalize claim evidence and build a defensible enrichment waterfall
paragraphs: The next four mapped plays are ERA Underpayment Triage, Remittance Code Explanation, QPA Disclosure Reconciliation, and Licensed Benchmark Enrichment. Begin with authorized X12 835 delivery through the provider's clearinghouse or payer channel. Preserve the original interchange and parse transaction, claim, service-line, adjustment, remark, and payment reference structures without flattening them prematurely. A CARC explains an adjustment category; it does not prove the payer violated the Act or that the claim belongs in federal IDR. RARCs add context but cannot replace the benefit document and actual notice. Track payer claim identifiers, service dates, modifiers, units, rendering NPI, location, and remittance trace references as distinct fields. Corrected claims and reversals must reference their predecessors. If 2,000 service lines arrive monthly and rules flag eight percent, 160 lines need review; at seven minutes each, the queue consumes about 18.7 hours before evidence collection. That is a staffing input, not 160 payable disputes. Route missing QPA disclosures to a document request, contradictory adjustments to analyst review, and suspected duplicates to a reconciliation queue. Never promote a code match directly into a demand packet without verifying the coverage and service circumstances.

The enrichment waterfall should spend progressively, stopping whenever a cheaper authoritative source answers the question. First use the engagement records, 835, explanation of benefits, and payer's required QPA disclosures. Next consult official identity and jurisdiction records. Then request missing encounter evidence from the provider through a secure channel. Only after eligibility is supportable should the desk buy licensed benchmark observations or commission clinical analysis. FAIR Health products can inform market context under their license terms; access to a website does not establish permission to scrape or redistribute a database. CMS Medicare schedules can help detect unit errors and implausible coding assumptions, but public-payer reimbursement rates are among the prohibited considerations in federal IDR determinations. Likewise, do not use usual-and-customary charges or billed charges as award-setting evidence. Keep those diagnostics outside the submitted merits packet. Offer construction must follow the current governing statute, operative rules, and applicable judicial decisions, rather than treating a benchmark multiplier as entitlement. If twenty eligible cases require an illustrative $35 licensed lookup allocation each, the enrichment budget is $700; if ten fail routing first, purchasing only the remaining ten saves $350 without sacrificing admissible evidence.

Treat HIPAA architecture as part of the data model. Execute Business Associate Agreements where required under 45 CFR §§ 164.502(e) and 164.504(e), and confirm that the selected vendor service, storage region, support access, and subcontracting arrangement are covered. A vendor's healthcare marketing page is not the agreement. Apply minimum-necessary access to caseworkers, segregate prospecting data from claim evidence, encrypt stored and transmitted records, and record access events without copying clinical narratives into ordinary application logs. HHS OCR's breach portal is a diligence signal about reported incidents, not a certification of current security. Use it to frame vendor questions rather than automatically rejecting every listed entity. Validate parsers against authorized test fixtures or genuinely synthetic examples before processing production remittances. A payment reversal, split remittance, duplicate interchange, negative adjustment, or changed claim identifier must produce an explainable result. Five fixtures covering those patterns are worth more than a dashboard showing thousands of untested rows. For restricted data, fallback means an approved provider transfer channel and manual structured extraction, not uploading the record to a public converter or general enrichment service. Retain required security documentation separately from the retention schedule chosen for the underlying claim artifacts.

sections.heading: 3. Control deadlines, portal evidence, and restrained commercial signals
paragraphs: The next three mapped plays are Open-Negotiation Deadline Control, IDR Portal Receipt Capture, and Cooling-Off Cohort Control. Model deadlines as events with evidence, not dates someone typed into a calendar. Under the federal framework, distinguish the window for initiating open negotiation after initial payment or denial from the thirty-business-day negotiation period itself. Then calculate the four-business-day initiation window following that period using the operative counting instructions and any applicable extensions. Certified entity selection is a separate procedural step; four business days is not a universal entity-selection or batching deadline. Capture the triggering notice, delivery method, receipt evidence, calculation version, holiday assumptions, and reviewer. Maintain both the statutory due date and an earlier internal target. If twelve cases approach a filing window and each needs twenty minutes of final verification, reserve four analyst hours before the internal target. Portal downtime does not automatically suspend a deadline. Preserve outage evidence and follow CMS's current documented assistance or extension process. Never treat an email to support as proof of a filed dispute. The fallback is a documented escalation using authorized channels, with the case visibly unresolved until an actual receipt exists.

Use the CMS Federal IDR portal as the submission system of record, not as an assumed general-purpose API. Do not invent a bulk endpoint or automate interactive credentials around portal restrictions. Capture confirmation identifiers, submitted versions, fee instructions, entity communications, and determinations through authorized access. Reconcile internal status to those artifacts daily during active filing windows. Cooling-off logic must attach the determination event to the relevant parties and same or similar items or services under the operative rule. Do not reduce every case to payer brand plus procedure code. Track the ninety-calendar-day restriction and the applicable subsequent initiation window separately; do not confuse this clock with the thirty-business-day negotiation clock. Batching needs its own dated eligibility test because governing rules and judicial decisions can change permissible grouping. Similar spreadsheet rows are not sufficient proof. At forty candidate lines, a proposed four-case batch may reduce duplicated preparation, but model four separate filings until grouping is confirmed. Fee savings belong in the forecast only after eligibility is documented. Google Calendar or Microsoft Outlook can mirror internal reminders, but the event ledger and preserved source documents must remain authoritative when reminders are edited or invitations fail.

The eleventh mapped play is saas_technographic_churn_pixel_scraping, applied only to permitted public commercial pages and DNS records for prospect timing, never patient-facing authenticated systems. Weekly comparisons can observe additions or removals of Salesforce, HubSpot, Marketo, Segment, or NetSuite indicators where those indicators are actually public. A weekly crawl cannot establish the exact installation day; retain an interval between the last negative and first positive observation. A removed script might reflect a tag-manager change, regional delivery, or site redesign rather than churn. Treat months ten through eleven after an observed installation as a weak outreach hypothesis, not a known annual renewal date. For 200 practice domains checked weekly, approximately 800 monthly page checks at an illustrative $0.02 allocated processing cost total $16; twenty ambiguous signals receiving eight minutes of review consume another 160 minutes. Those figures exclude commercial license charges and are not vendor quotes. Confirm apparent switches with passive DNS TXT/CNAME history and public job-posting mentions before routing outreach. Stop on access restrictions, cache results, and never use this play as evidence of claim eligibility, clinical acuity, payer behavior, or collectible IDR proceeds.

callout.title: Verify four facts before the filing package leaves the desk
callout.body: A complete packet needs a supported jurisdiction decision, a defensible clock, permissible evidence, and a case-level cash model.
items: Confirm coverage, service circumstances, applicable state payment rules, and federal eligibility from encounter-specific documents rather than payer branding.
Recompute negotiation and initiation deadlines from preserved triggering events, current counting instructions, and documented extensions.
Check batching eligibility, cooling-off relationships, entity status, and the current fee schedule using dated official sources.
Remove prohibited award-setting considerations and verify that expected contingency earnings depend on incremental collected cash after unrecovered fees and casework allocations.

sections.heading: 4. Reconcile collections, test failure modes, and protect the scorecard
paragraphs: The twelfth mapped play is Cash-Verified Contingency Reconciliation. Build its ledger around money received, not offers selected. Suppose the payer initially paid $1,200, an IDR determination sets total payment at $4,200, and only $2,400 of the additional $3,000 has actually arrived. Collected incremental cash is $2,400; the remaining $600 stays a receivable and earns no contingency fee under this model. For illustration, allocate $120 of non-refundable administrative expense, $80 of other unrecovered case fees, and $200 of casework to the collected increment. These are modeling amounts, not the current CMS fee schedule. The distributable recovery basis is $2,000; a 25% contractual operator share earns $500. Record certified entity fee deposits separately while disposition is pending. Return of the prevailing party's deposit must be supported by the applicable procedure and actual refund evidence; losing or ineligible-case deposits must not become assumed refunds. Treat unrecovered amounts as costs unless a documented refund right supports a receivable. Define who advances expenses, how recoveries reimburse them, and which casework charges reduce the sharing basis. A dollar allocated before the split cannot also be deducted a second time from the same operator earnings calculation.

Formula v2.0 remains fixed despite the illustrative case arithmetic. Conservative recognized operator revenue is $110,000, allowable total operator expense is $77,000, and owner net profit is $33,000 at 30%. Base revenue is $505,000, expense is $287,850, and profit is $217,150 at 43.0%. Scaled revenue is $900,000, expense is $396,000, and profit is $504,000 at 56%. These figures exclude initial provider collections, payer principal, uncollected awards, and recoveries belonging to the provider. At the illustrative $500 earned share per completed collection equivalent, the revenue targets require 220, 1,010, and 1,800 equivalents annually. They are collection equivalents, not required filing counts or promised outcomes. If only 80% of otherwise comparable completed matters reach that collection level during the year, illustrative work volumes rise to 275, about 1,263, and 2,250 matters respectively. Test whether the assigned 1 FT + 2 C, 1 FT + 2 C, and 2 FT + 3 C teams can support those queues. Apply principal-versus-agent analysis under ASC 606 to actual contracts; the scorecard here counts earned operator shares, not gross provider recoveries passed through an account. Maintain separate expense buckets so case allocations and operator overhead reconcile without duplicate deductions.

Turn the scorecard into a diagnostic dashboard with four independent measures: evidence completeness, procedural timeliness, earned revenue, and cash aging. Do not combine them into a single success percentage. An eligible, timely, prevailing dispute can still have an unpaid balance. Match supplemental ERAs to bank deposits and provider posting records, then flag unmatched receipts, recoupments, reversals, and cross-claim offsets before issuing the contingency invoice. Use SQLite for a small local reconciliation prototype or PostgreSQL for a controlled multiuser ledger; neither product choice substitutes for access restrictions, backup testing, and audit history. Keep protected records out of source control, telemetry exports, and prospecting systems. Test recovery from a backup using a restricted environment and document elapsed restoration time. A nightly job should produce an exception count, oldest unresolved age, and named owner, not merely a green execution status. Review the eight controls below weekly and before every material parser or rule change. If an input feed fails, freeze affected decisions while preserving unaffected work. The useful automation boundary is precise: software assembles traceable evidence and calculations; accountable staff resolve disputed facts, confirm submissions, and authorize collection-based billing only after the underlying cash movement is matched.

chapters.executive_summary: Candidate #45, Rank #09 of 49, earns a 94/100 Money-to-Manpower Score by turning eligible out-of-network underpayments into documented, collected provider recoveries. This chapter organizes 12 mapped plays into jurisdiction, licensing, privacy, scope, fee calculation, asset ownership, liability, calendars, evidence, cash reconciliation, outbound infrastructure, and discovery. The canonical annual owner-profit cases are $33,000 Conservative, $217,150 Base, and $504,000 Scaled; revenue means earned contingency shares, never provider medical billings. Execute the business associate agreement before transferring protected records, establish federal versus state jurisdiction before spending filing fees, and invoice only on incremental cash after specified costs. Outreach must use legitimately provisioned accounts, truthful claims, and durable suppression rather than disposable identities or promised recoveries.

sections.heading: 1. Establish jurisdiction, licensing boundaries, and protected-data authority
paragraphs: Play 1, jurisdiction routing, starts with the service and plan, not the payer logo. Obtain the service date, place of service, provider network status, plan funding evidence, initial payment or denial, and applicable state payment rules. The federal framework in 42 U.S.C. § 300gg-111 addresses specified emergency services and certain nonemergency services furnished by nonparticipating providers at participating facilities; air ambulance disputes have a separate statutory provision. Ground ambulance bills do not become federal IDR cases merely because they are out of network. A specified state law or applicable All-Payer Model Agreement can determine the payment route instead. ERISA preemption under 29 U.S.C. § 1144 is important, but an ERISA label alone does not settle every claim's jurisdiction. Funding status, state opt-in arrangements, service category, and the law's actual reach matter. Store the evidence supporting each routing decision rather than inferring self-funding from an 835 transaction. New York and Texas illustrate why one national payer can administer claims governed by different dispute systems. If evidence conflicts, obtain plan documentation and a written routing determination before incurring an entity fee. Separately evaluate balance-billing protection; federal arbitration eligibility and patient protections are related but not interchangeable determinations.

Play 2, licensing and representation, separates administrative recovery work from practicing law, collecting consumer debts, and selling clinical referrals. A provider authorization should identify the business acting as its representative, permitted portal actions, negotiation authority, and who can accept a settlement. That authorization does not create a law license or override a state's collection-agency requirements. Florida's commercial collection regime, including Fla. Stat. § 559.553, deserves a specific applicability review when the proposed activity involves collecting commercial claims. New York Judiciary Law §§ 478 and 484 illustrate separate restrictions on unauthorized legal practice. Have qualified local counsel classify activities by provider location, business location, debtor relationship, and forum; do not assume that calling the service analytics changes its substance. Escalate litigation, subpoenas, disputed legal interpretation, and contested ERISA benefit litigation to retained counsel. Analyze percentage fees under applicable professional fee-splitting rules rather than declaring every contingency arrangement permissible. Where federal healthcare program business is implicated, assess 42 U.S.C. § 1320a-7b(b) before compensating referral sources. Keep marketing compensation independent of patient referrals and treatment volume. The practical fallback is a narrower administrative scope, a properly licensed service partner, or declining the affected work while preserving the provider's remaining filing time.

Play 3, privacy authority, requires an executed HIPAA business associate agreement before the recovery operator receives protected health information on the provider's behalf. Pair 45 CFR § 164.504(e) with Security Rule safeguards under 45 CFR §§ 164.308 and 164.312, and apply minimum-necessary access under § 164.502(b) where applicable. The services agreement alone is insufficient. Specify permitted payment and operations uses, incident reporting, subcontractor restrictions, return or destruction, and treatment of records that must be retained. Use individual accounts, multifactor authentication, encrypted transfer, and access logs; keep prospecting tools outside the clinical-record boundary. Microsoft 365 or a cloud storage brand is not proof that a particular product, subscription, and configuration are covered by the required contractual commitments. Verify those commitments for each service receiving records. An 835 ERA can contain sensitive identifiers even when the attachment lacks a clinical narrative. Collect only claim fields necessary for screening, then obtain selected clinical evidence through the controlled workspace. Evaluate additional restrictions before accepting substance-use-disorder records governed by 42 CFR Part 2. If a prospect emails records prematurely, restrict access, notify the designated privacy contact, and follow the documented incident process instead of forwarding the attachment into a sales sequence.

sections.heading: 2. Contract for collected uplift, controlled authority, and clean ownership
paragraphs: Play 4, contractual scope, defines the service as screening, authorized negotiation, eligible IDR administration, evidence assembly, and cash reconciliation for listed provider entities and claim populations. Attach the tax identifiers, specialties, service periods, excluded payers, and excluded litigation activities. State who funds administrative fees, entity fees, clinical review, and external counsel; require express budget authority before expanding a matter. Give the operator limited representation authority rather than unrestricted power to bind the practice. Settlement instructions should identify minimum acceptable terms and the person authorized to change them. Play 5, the fee trigger, defines baseline collections as the payer's actual initial allowed payment allocated to the claim, not the QPA disclosure when those amounts differ. Incremental recovery excludes baseline receipts, patient cost sharing, unrelated claim payments, and uncollected awards. Deduct the agreed nonrefundable administrative charges, unrecovered entity fees, and attributable casework costs before applying the contingency percentage. Attach a worked example and a claim-level reconciliation format. Define treatment of interest, partial receipts, recoupments, refunds, and bundled remittances explicitly. A favorable determination creates a collection task; it does not by itself establish an earned cash-triggered contingency invoice or authority to debit the provider's bank account.

Use a precise waterfall: eligible incremental cash equals reconciled payer cash attributable to the recovery minus baseline payments already included in that total; subtract unrecovered filing charges and agreed casework costs; floor the resulting contingency base at zero. For example, a $4,000 initial payment followed by $10,000 additional cash creates $10,000 of incremental receipts, not $14,000 of fee basis. If actual unrecovered charges are $750 and attributable casework costs are $1,250, the net recovery base is $8,000. A 25% contingency produces $2,000 of operator revenue and $6,000 of provider residual benefit after those costs. The $750 is an illustrative combined ledger amount, not a quoted CMS fee schedule. If the operator also incurs $400 of nonreimbursed overhead allocated to that engagement, its contribution is $1,600. Track reimbursed advances through the appropriate clearing accounts and evaluate principal versus agent presentation under ASC 606; never count the provider's recovery as operator revenue. Where the operator bears a case expense rather than obtaining reimbursement, record that expense consistently and do not deduct it twice in the profit bridge. A later entity-fee refund changes unrecovered costs and requires a transparent true-up.

Play 6, asset ownership, assigns provider records, claim decisions, and matter-specific deliverables to the agreed owner while reserving reusable software and general templates to the operator. Ownership language does not itself authorize secondary use of protected information. Restrict training, resale, and cross-client benchmarking unless separately permitted under applicable contracts and privacy rules. Play 7, liability and dispute design, makes anti-circumvention a narrow collection-reporting obligation covering identified worked claims for a defined tail period. It should not capture unrelated future collections or obstruct provider access to records. Require receipt reporting, reasonable audit access, and cooperation after termination. A liability cap should specify its monetary basis and deliberate exceptions for fraud, willful misconduct, confidentiality breaches, and other negotiated exposures; evaluate enforceability under the selected state's law. Align indemnities with responsibility for inaccurate source records, unauthorized submissions, and security incidents. Define notice, cure, venue, governing law, emergency relief, and mediation or arbitration for disputes between operator and provider. Keep that private contract mechanism distinct from statutory payer-provider IDR. On termination, deliver the deadline register, submission receipts, pending determinations, payment ledger, and authorized record export. Invoice disputes should never become an excuse to hide a live filing deadline or withhold essential transition information.

sections.heading: 3. Operate versioned calendars, defensible submissions, and cash controls
paragraphs: Play 8, deadline control, implements distinct clocks instead of one generic thirty-day task. Under the baseline federal process, a party generally initiates open negotiation within 30 business days after receiving the initial payment or denial. The open-negotiation period then lasts 30 business days; federal IDR generally must be initiated within four business days after that period ends. The four-day window is not a universal entity-selection or batching deadline. Record receipt evidence, negotiation delivery, calendar definitions, holidays, portal acknowledgments, and any authorized extension. Implement the clock in a versioned state machine with a second-person check rather than trusting a spreadsheet formula copied between jurisdictions. The 90-calendar-day cooling-off restriction concerns the initiating party bringing subsequent disputes involving the same other party and same or similar items or services after a determination; it is not a blanket ninety-day suspension of all payer work. The statute also provides a subsequent initiation opportunity for affected claims. Maintain a linked cooling-off register and calculate the applicable post-period window. Check current regulations, controlling court orders, and CMS implementation instructions before relying on operational batching criteria or portal procedures. Store the version used, because a historically correct workflow can become wrong after an implementation change.

Play 9, evidence construction, distinguishes permissible claim-specific support from prohibited arbitration inputs. The statute directs consideration of the QPA and specified additional information, while excluding usual and customary charges, billed charges, and public-program reimbursement rates as payment determinants. Do not instruct a brief builder to multiply a FAIR Health charge percentile and present the result as a permissible federal IDR valuation. Identify the licensed dataset, its actual measure, the evidentiary proposition, and whether that use is permissible before including any benchmark. Clinical acuity, patient complexity, training, facility characteristics, and documented contracting efforts need claim-specific support and careful treatment of information already reflected in the QPA. CARC and RARC values help classify remittances but cannot prove jurisdiction, clinical complexity, or an incorrect QPA independently. Use templates to assemble exhibits, then require a qualified reviewer to verify every assertion and source. For batching, evaluate the operative statutory and regulatory conditions, including relevant party, service, coding, and service-period requirements, rather than assuming one payer name makes all claims compatible. When compatibility is uncertain, split supported cases or obtain clarification before filing. A cheaper aggregate submission is expensive if dismissal destroys its expected recovery and consumes unrecoverable fees.

Play 10, cash reconciliation, tracks submitted offer, determination, payment due date, actual receipt, fee refund, and recoupment as different ledger events. The federal statute generally requires payment within 30 calendar days after the determination; an overdue award belongs in a documented collection escalation, not in cash revenue. The administrative fee is nonrefundable. In an ordinary completed determination, the prevailing party's advanced entity fee is generally returned while the nonprevailing party bears that fee. Dismissals, withdrawals, settlements, and eligibility failures require the applicable fee terms and current instructions; do not assume a refund merely because the merits were never reached. Budget ineligible dismissals as potential entity-fee forfeitures. The canonical annual bridge remains $110,000 revenue less $77,000 total operator expense equals $33,000 owner profit; $505,000 less $287,850 equals $217,150; and $900,000 less $396,000 equals $504,000. These are 30%, 43.0%, and 56% margins with teams of 1 FT plus 2 C, 1 FT plus 2 C, and 2 FT plus 3 C. At an illustrative 25% fee, those revenues require $440,000, $2,020,000, and $3,600,000 of net incremental collected fee bases. Neither favorable offer statistics nor pending awards establish those cash volumes; report both collection delays and unrecovered case costs explicitly.

sections.heading: 4. Use lawful outbound infrastructure and exact provider discovery language
paragraphs: Play 11 is multi_inbox_free_workspace_outbound_clusters, the mapped TRACK_2 outbound infrastructure play. Its proposed capacity math is straightforward: 300 authorized inboxes sending 15 to 25 messages across 20 working days produce 90,000 to 150,000 attempted messages monthly. At retail prices of $6 to $12 per seat, 300 seats cost $1,800 to $3,600 monthly before domains and relay charges. Subsidized Microsoft 365 developer or partner accounts may be used only when actual eligibility and product terms expressly permit the intended production sending; free access is not assumed. Cloudflare Email Routing handles forwarding, not a substitute outbound SMTP service. Use a relay that explicitly permits the campaign type and configure sender authentication. Keeping two or three domains per legitimately provisioned tenant is a management limit, not permission to evade provider restrictions. Remove open and click pixels, centralize suppression, and verify address quality through an authorized service. SMTP catch-all responses cannot certify every mailbox or guarantee delivery. Maintain standby domains only for approved continuity with stable identity and suppression, never to evade blocks. If subsidies or acceptable-use terms fail, reduce volume and purchase permitted service. No inbox-count formula establishes primary-folder placement, positive replies, or collected recovery revenue.

CAN-SPAM, 15 U.S.C. § 7704, applies to commercial business-to-business email as well as consumer campaigns. Use accurate headers, a nondeceptive subject, the required advertising identification, a valid postal address, and a working opt-out; honor requests within ten business days and suppress them across every sending identity. Retain the suppression record rather than reimporting an opted-out address from another vendor. Outsourcing the send does not eliminate the advertiser's responsibilities. Address verification is a deliverability control, not recipient permission. Do not use harvested lists obtained through prohibited methods or buy lists whose provenance cannot be explained. For phone discovery, distinguish manual calls from automated dialing, prerecorded messages, and texts; evaluate 47 U.S.C. § 227, implementing FCC rules, applicable state restrictions, and the recipient's number type before selecting a channel. A practice manager's mobile number is not automatically an unrestricted business line. Avoid patient-facing solicitations and never put patient identifiers in outreach. Campaign economics must include verification, domains, permitted mail service, suppression operations, and staff review, not merely seat savings. If 150,000 attempted messages yield an illustrative 0.2% positive response rate, that is 300 responses, not 300 qualified practices or engagements. Scale only after measuring legitimate opportunities and staff capacity.

Play 12, discovery and handoff, converts a response into a bounded eligibility conversation, not an award prediction. Use this opening verbatim: 'We help provider groups evaluate eligible out-of-network payment disputes and administer authorized recovery work. We charge an agreed share of incremental cash actually collected after specified unrecovered fees and case costs. Could we discuss your specialty, service states, payer products, and current dispute workflow without sharing patient information?' Then ask: 'Who owns your initial-payment records, open-negotiation calendar, and settlement authority, and how do you distinguish self-funded plans from insured products?' Explain the handoff directly: 'Please do not email patient records. If the scope fits, we will execute the services agreement and business associate agreement, then provide the controlled intake method.' For outcome questions, say: 'We can model eligibility, costs, and collection timing after reviewing the records; a favorable determination and actual payment are separate events.' End with a specific next action: 'May we schedule twenty minutes with your revenue-cycle owner and review aggregate claim counts first?' Record objections and exclusions in the CRM, never diagnoses or member identifiers. If the prospect declines, acknowledge the request and suppress further promotional contact across the cluster.

sections.heading: 1. Build an evidence-first intake spine before adding language models
paragraphs: Start with a tenant-isolated intake spine, not a chatbot attached to a clearinghouse export. Receive authorized 835 ERA files, associated 837 claim records, payer correspondence, and plan documents through an authenticated transfer channel. Execute HIPAA Business Associate Agreements with covered-entity clients and applicable downstream service providers before transmitting protected health information. Python parses transaction envelopes, CLP claim records, SVC service lines, CAS adjustments, and remark-code references into a versioned claim ledger. Match CARC and RARC combinations against dated code dictionaries; never interpret every contractual adjustment as recoverable underpayment. Preserve original bytes, source hashes, parser version, receipt timestamp, and the relationship between claim and service line. A PostgreSQL record stores operational state; encrypted object storage holds evidence with access logging and tested retention controls. Signed webhooks enqueue identifiers rather than clinical narratives. Duplicate files produce the same ingestion key, while corrected remittances create linked versions instead of silently overwriting evidence. The employee owns exceptions and client authority; one contractor reconciles claims; the other prepares evidence. This division lets machines normalize thousands of lines without giving a model discretion to classify disputed jurisdiction or authorize an external filing.

Treat the ERISA classifier as an evidence router with an abstention state. An employer name, insurer logo, or 835 payer identifier cannot establish whether a plan is self-funded, fully insured, subject to a specified state law, or affected by an applicable All-Payer Model Agreement. Collect the summary plan description, funding evidence, service location, service date, provider status, and the relevant emergency or nonemergency service facts. Record state opt-in evidence when that mechanism matters. ERISA section 514, codified at 29 U.S.C. § 1144, supplies a framework rather than a shortcut that sends every employer claim to federal IDR. A rules engine proposes a route and names missing documents; a reviewer signs the route before fees are exposed. Maintain separate queues for federal candidates, state-process candidates, ordinary payment disputes, and unresolved evidence. For language-model extraction, require a structured object containing source page, quoted support, proposed field, and uncertainty reason. Reject unsupported values instead of filling gaps with plausible answers. Claims containing instructions inside attachments remain evidence, never executable workflow commands. A low-confidence result returns to document collection, not directly to the arbitration portal.

The chapter's 12-play map uses eleven local implementation labels plus the supplied distribution play identifier; the local labels are operating modules, not additional canonical catalog claims. Plays one through four are era_evidence_normalization, jurisdiction_evidence_router, deadline_event_ledger, and idempotent_work_dispatch. Each module owns a measurable input, output, exception queue, and human override record. Measure the automation objective using a frozen catalog of repetitive task instances. In an illustrative thousand-task week, 740 tasks complete without manual rework and 260 require intervention: 740 divided by 1,000 equals 74%. Do not inflate the numerator with retries or split one extraction into dozens of trivial events. If those tasks previously required four minutes each, automated completion removes 2,960 gross minutes, before quality sampling, maintenance, and exception handling. Audit 10% of automated completions initially, with heavier sampling for new payers and changed formats. Any material jurisdiction error pauses that rule version and replays affected records into review. Track minutes as a second measure because automating many cheap classifications can conceal expensive brief corrections. The target becomes credible only when rework-adjusted labor and missed-deadline rates improve together.

callout.title: Four intake habits that prevent expensive false positives
callout.body: The strongest automation advantage is refusing weak evidence before an ineligible dispute consumes fees and reviewer time.
items: Keep corrected 835 transactions linked to their predecessors; a replacement remittance must not create a second recovery opportunity.
Request plan funding evidence during onboarding, because an insurer's administrative-services role can resemble ordinary insured coverage.
Store negotiation delivery evidence separately from the drafted letter; a generated PDF proves preparation, not receipt or timely initiation.
Sample CARC/RARC patterns by payer and service class, because one global underpayment rule can multiply a coding mistake across every client.

sections.heading: 2. Turn statutory clocks into tested state transitions and controlled dispatch
paragraphs: Build the deadline engine around distinct events rather than a single thirty-day timer. Under the applicable federal framework, the initiating party generally must start open negotiation within thirty business days after receiving the initial payment or notice of denial. The open-negotiation period itself runs thirty business days beginning on its initiation date. A federal IDR initiation generally follows within four business days after that period ends. These are different clocks, and the four-day window is not a universal deadline for choosing the certified entity or assembling every batch. Encode each requirement from the effective version of 45 CFR § 149.510 and applicable official implementation instructions. Preserve the source receipt date, counting convention, holiday calendar version, local time context, computed deadline, and reviewer confirmation. Use states such as received, evidence_pending, route_confirmed, negotiation_sent, negotiation_elapsed, initiation_ready, initiated, offer_pending, determination_received, and cash_reconciled. A clock continues while evidence is missing; moving a claim into a document queue does not suspend a statutory deadline. Escalate approaching deadlines to two people and show the exact missing action, not a generic red badge.

Plays five through eight are batch_eligibility_matcher, permitted_evidence_builder, offer_packet_validator, and award_cash_reconciler. Batch matching must evaluate the effective legal criteria, not simply combine claims sharing a payer and CPT family. Store the initiating and opposing parties, qualified items or services, service dates, and every criterion supporting aggregation. The same-party, same-or-similar-item cooling-off restriction generally spans ninety calendar days after a determination; affected claims require separate tracking, including the applicable post-suspension initiation opportunity. Do not stop negotiation preparation merely because initiation is temporarily restricted. Version rules against current agency implementation and operative court decisions before using them on live claims. A scheduled Python worker queries due actions, acquires a transactional lease, writes an outbox event, and dispatches only approved actions. Webhook acknowledgments update delivery state, while official portal confirmations establish submission status. A timeout means status unresolved, not permission to file again. If portal access fails, preserve screenshots, timestamps, and support correspondence; follow the official extension process when available. An outage does not itself extend a deadline, and a model must never invent that relief.

Budget the machine layer by completed run and separate it from reviewer labor. An illustrative intake run costs $0.003 in parsing compute, $0.004 in queue and database usage, $0.006 in OCR, and $0.015 in bounded extraction: $0.028 total under the assumed allocation. Ten thousand runs therefore cost $280 before storage, fixed subscriptions, and human review. If 5% require one full retry, 500 additional runs add $14, producing $294 or $0.0294 per original record. Vendor prices, document lengths, and OCR incidence must replace these planning assumptions during measurement. A three-minute review at $45 per hour costs $2.25, so preventing unnecessary review matters far more than shaving a fraction of a cent from tokens. Apply bounded retries only to transient technical failures. Invalid jurisdiction, missing authorization, contradictory receipts, and unsupported clinical assertions require people. A dead-letter queue carries the source hash, failed operation, next deadline, and named owner. Run nightly reconciliation between queue records and portal receipts. Test holidays, duplicate callbacks, out-of-order messages, daylight-saving transitions, corrected remittances, and worker crashes before expanding the automated population. Keep a manual deadline register ready for infrastructure outages.

sections.heading: 3. Generate permitted evidence, then reconcile awards to actual incremental cash
paragraphs: The brief builder should resemble a cited evidence compiler, not an advocate allowed to invent facts. Play six retrieves the QPA supplied for the disputed service, documented clinical acuity, provider training and experience where relevant, facility characteristics where applicable, and supported contracting history. A language model drafts only from approved excerpts and returns a source map for every factual assertion. Licensed FAIR Health material requires especially careful separation: its usual-and-customary charge benchmarks cannot become an arbitration anchor merely because the data are commercially reputable. Federal IDR excludes specified considerations, including usual and customary charges, billed charges, and public-payer reimbursement rates. Use any licensed product only for a permitted purpose consistent with its terms and the governing evidentiary rules; otherwise exclude it from the offer packet. Distinguish operational opportunity screening from evidence actually submitted. Do not assume the QPA carries a conclusive presumption or automatically determines the result. Current operative rules and court decisions govern consideration of permissible information. Human reviewers test whether each acuity assertion explains this service and avoids double counting factors already reflected in the QPA.

Play seven validates the final-offer packet because baseball arbitration selects between party offers rather than inviting the model to manufacture a compromise award. Keep the requested amount, initial payment, service identifiers, offer rationale, and supporting exhibits mutually consistent. A clinical reviewer confirms acuity and service facts; the authorized case lead approves the offer and submission. Generate a PDF with stable exhibit numbers and verify that every cited page exists. Use a bounded model for extraction and a stronger model only for complex drafting, both inside appropriately contracted environments with documented retention and training controls. An illustrative packet costs $0.18 for extraction, $0.42 for drafting, and $0.10 for rendering and validation: $0.70 in variable machine spend. Twelve minutes of review at $60 per hour adds $12, making $12.70 before allocated subscriptions and filing costs. If two of twenty packets require ten extra review minutes each, the cohort adds $20 and averages $13.70 per packet. Reject unsupported citations, contradictory amounts, and missing exhibits automatically. After repeated drafting failure, switch to the approved template and human completion rather than sending a weaker packet to preserve throughput.

Play eight reconciles determinations to bank-confirmed incremental collections, because a favorable offer statistic is not a cash conversion rate. Suppose matched claims originally paid $100,000 and eventually show $160,000 in cumulative payer collections. Incremental cash is $60,000, not $160,000 and not an unpaid award balance. Deduct $10,000 of non-refundable CMS administrative fees, unrecovered certified-entity fees, and direct casework costs to obtain a $50,000 eligible fee pool. At a contracted 25% contingency, operator revenue is $12,500. Track prevailing-party entity-fee refunds as receivables until returned; losing or ineligibility-dismissed disputes retain their forfeited fees in cost reconciliation under the applicable rules. CMS administrative fees remain separate and non-refundable. Do not deduct the same casework expense again in company profit if it was borne and recorded as a provider-level fee-base deduction; operator-borne expenses still belong in the operator ledger. Age awarded-but-unpaid balances and pursue documented payment follow-up, including the applicable thirty-calendar-day payment requirement. Never invoice an earned cash contingency merely because a determination arrived. Reverse or adjust invoices for linked recoupments according to the signed engagement terms.

sections.heading: 4. Compound permission-led distribution without breaking the cash model
paragraphs: Plays nine through twelve are high_velocity_dm_outbound_systems, provider_referral_loop, jurisdiction_content_engine, and cohort_margin_feedback. Implement the supplied TRACK_2 high-velocity play with user-initiated comment, reaction, or inbound-message triggers rather than blind mass DM campaigns. Publish a practical negotiation-deadline worksheet and invite practice administrators to request it. Use only platform-supported messaging features and permitted integrations; where an automated response is unsupported, queue a human reply. Route warm signals among authorized inboxes by territory and existing relationship, never to bypass platform restrictions. Require an actual prospect reply before sending external links, and move claim documents to the approved secure intake channel. In an illustrative monthly cohort, 120 qualifying triggers produce 72 replies, 24 discovery calls, eight authorized samples, and two engagements. With $480 in content and messaging spend plus twelve hours at $45, acquisition cost is $1,020 divided by two, or $510 per signed engagement. These are planning conversions, not measured results. PeerFloodError, delivery suppression, or repeated message-request silence stops automated dispatch and returns the team to permission capture rather than account rotation. Honor opt-outs across every authorized inbox and client-acquisition list.

The referral loop distributes operational proof, not patient stories. Give billing firms, practice-management consultants, and specialty associations a shareable worksheet explaining receipt evidence, jurisdiction documents, and incremental-cash accounting. Referral compensation is not required for this loop; any proposed payment arrangement needs separate assessment under the rules applicable to its parties and services. Programmatic pages should answer narrow operator questions such as how to distinguish a negotiation clock from an initiation clock, with human-checked primary citations and an update date. Publish no payer-specific recovery claim without a defensible denominator and actual collection data. Aggregate reporting still requires a disclosure-risk assessment; remove identifying details using an appropriate HIPAA de-identification method rather than merely deleting patient names. One approved worksheet can generate an association presentation, a search landing page, and an inbound request sequence. Track source, qualified sample, signed engagement, first collected contingency, and retained contribution as separate events. A signed client that supplies only ineligible claims is acquisition failure, not growth. Feed disqualification reasons back into page copy and intake questions, then preserve useful pages instead of generating hundreds of thin specialty variants.

Close the flywheel with the exact Formula v2.0 scorecard rather than optimistic award multiples. At an illustrative uniform 25% contingency, eligible annual cash pools after the specified direct deductions of $440,000, $2,020,000, and $3,600,000 produce operator revenue of $110,000, $505,000, and $900,000. These pools are reverse-engineered planning requirements, not forecasts of claim eligibility or collection success. Conservative company expenses of $77,000 leave $33,000 owner profit at 30%; Base expenses of $287,850 leave $217,150 at 43.0%; Scaled expenses of $396,000 leave $504,000 at 56%. Conservative and Base each use one full-time employee plus two contractors; Scaled uses two full-time employees plus three contractors. Reconcile every expense category to this company-level bridge without double counting provider-borne deductions. The $1,800–$10,500 monthly operating range is an operating-budget reference, not the entire annual expense denominator for all scenarios. Budget $10,000–$45,000 startup capital and a one-to-four-month first-deal interval, while separately funding fee advances and delayed collections. Increase distribution only when deadline reliability, review capacity, and collected cohort contribution remain healthy. Additional leads cannot repair a cash-starved recovery operation.

chapters.question_prompt: How do you structure a lean 1 FT + 2 C (3 people) -> 2 FT + 3 C (5 people) pod, enforce weekly scorecards, and build transferable books that command a premium exit multiple (or durable cash cow)?
chapters.title: Pod Architecture, Contractor KPIs & Exit Valuation
chapters.subtitle: Three-to-Five-Person IDR Pods, Cash-Verified Contingency Waterfalls, HIPAA Controls, and Transferable Recovery Books
chapters.executive_summary: Candidate #45, ranked #09 of 49 with a 94/100 Money-to-Manpower Score, turns out-of-network recovery into a transferable operating book only when deadlines, evidence, collections, and ownership survive the founder. This chapter organizes 12 mapped plays into a three-person pod, then adds two seats only when measured workload supports them. Canonical annual owner profits are $33,000 Conservative, $217,150 Base, and $504,000 Scaled; operator revenue excludes initial payer collections and uncollected awards. Weekly scorecards connect jurisdiction screening, filing quality, fee exposure, payer aging, and cash realization. Contractor incentives reward accepted work rather than speculative awards. Concentration limits, documented intellectual-property ownership, reproducible cohort ledgers, and founder replacement costs determine whether the book deserves a stronger exit valuation or remains a durable cash-producing operation.

sections.heading: 1. Assign Twelve Recovery Plays to Named Seats Before Adding Headcount
paragraphs: Build the initial pod around one full-time accountable operator and two specialist contractors, not three interchangeable claim processors. The operator owns provider relationships, jurisdiction exceptions, cash reconciliation, and the weekly queue. Contractor A owns intake and deadline operations; Contractor B owns evidence assembly, offer support, and submission quality. Use this chapter's twelve-play operating map: P01 provider qualification, P02 engagement and BAA execution, P03 835 ingestion, P04 jurisdiction classification, P05 incremental-recovery screening, P06 open negotiation, P07 IDR initiation and entity selection, P08 batching and cooling-off control, P09 evidence and offer assembly, P10 determination tracking, P11 remittance reconciliation, and P12 renewal and book transfer. These are assigned workstreams, not twelve additional jobs. The operator retains accountability for every play while delegating production through explicit acceptance criteria. Federal eligibility under 42 U.S.C. section 300gg-111 depends on the service, coverage, and applicable payment regime; an ERISA label alone does not establish the correct route. Capture plan funding, service location, provider specialty, service category, and applicable state payment rules before spending entity fees. Store the classification rationale alongside source documents so another reviewer can reproduce the decision without interviewing the founder. Escalate unresolved jurisdiction questions before filing, rather than rewarding a contractor for sending an unsupported case.

Run the deadline engine as a controlled state machine with an assigned owner, backup, timestamp, and delivery evidence for every transition. The ordinary federal sequence includes initiating open negotiation within the applicable thirty-business-day window after initial payment or denial, completing the thirty-business-day negotiation period, and initiating IDR within four business days after that period ends. The four-day window is not a blanket deadline for every entity-selection or batching task. Configure later milestones separately under the operative version of 45 CFR section 149.510 and applicable extensions. Use PostgreSQL for the event ledger and a private task interface for assignments; retain portal confirmations in an access-controlled document store. A calendar reminder without acknowledged service is not completion evidence. Contractor A prepares notices and verifies addresses; Contractor B checks disputed dates and submission attachments; the operator resolves exceptions. Record holidays, timezone conventions, outages, and corrected inputs in an append-only audit history. For P08, explicitly record the parties, item or service classification, determination date, and relevant ninety-calendar-day cooling-off restriction. Do not pool unrelated provider claims merely because a payer name matches. Require an independent batch-eligibility check before submission and preserve the rule version applied.

Move to two full-time seats and three contractors only when accepted workload, rather than gross award announcements, exceeds demonstrated capacity. The original operator becomes portfolio and commercial lead; the second employee becomes production and quality lead. Retain the intake contractor and evidence contractor, then add a remittance and exception-resolution contractor for P10 and P11. This is five people in total, not five employees plus a hidden service bureau. Budget specialist consultations separately and disclose their expense without representing occasional advice as a permanent production seat. Measure touch minutes by play for four weeks, then estimate committed capacity after leave, rework, and deadline reserves. An illustrative eighty-percent utilization ceiling leaves room for short filing windows and payer exceptions; it is an operating target, not a statutory requirement. Every critical play needs a trained backup, but a person's backup assignment does not create extra capacity. Execute HIPAA business associate agreements and applicable subcontractor agreements before protected information moves, with role-based access and auditable offboarding. Keep provider files inside contracted systems rather than personal inboxes. Document a two-week founder-absence exercise before expansion: another named person must run the queue, reconcile cash, and explain unresolved exceptions from the records alone.

callout.title: Protect the Thin Pod From Expensive Recovery Friction
callout.body: The highest-value efficiencies remove preventable rework without weakening jurisdiction, evidence, or cash verification.
items: Keep an immutable copy of each original 835 and corrected remittance; payer adjustments can otherwise erase the initial-payment baseline used for contingency calculations.
Prebuild specialty-specific evidence indexes, but make the reviewer confirm patient-specific acuity and permitted factors before reusing any argument.
Maintain a separate cooling-off register keyed to the relevant parties and item or service classification; a payer-wide calendar entry is too coarse.
Assign every determination a remittance owner immediately; a favorable offer selection does not deposit money or establish an earned contingency.

sections.heading: 2. Pay Contractors for Accepted Work and Publish One Weekly Scorecard
paragraphs: Contractor compensation should purchase defined outputs without encouraging ineligible filings or inflated offers. For planning, use illustrative hourly rates of $35 to $55 for intake work and $65 to $95 for specialized evidence work, then validate actual proposals against the expense envelope. A piece-rate alternative should specify exactly what an accepted package contains, how revisions are handled, and which disputed tasks remain billable. Pay for properly documented ineligibility findings as well as eligible packages; otherwise the contractor has an economic reason to suppress bad news. Avoid bonuses based solely on award size, portal submissions, or headline prevailing rates. A modest quality component can reward timely, accepted work and accurate reconciliations, with exclusions for payer delay outside the contractor's control. Define a one-business-day acknowledgment target, a two-business-day routine defect correction target, and same-day escalation for deadlines inside five business days. These are internal service targets, not substitutes for statutory clocks. Have the reviewer identify the defect category and affected claim instead of returning a vague rejection. Specify correction economics in the statement of work, and avoid unilateral payment deductions. Worker classification follows actual relationships and applicable law; a contractor label does not settle employee status.

Publish the scorecard at the same weekly cutoff using stable denominators and claim-level drilldowns. For P03 through P05, show complete-intake rate, independently confirmed eligibility rate, and screening turnaround. For P06 through P08, show notices served on time, initiation deadlines met, rejected submissions, and preventable ineligibility dismissals. For P09, show first-pass acceptance, hours per accepted brief, and defects by evidence category. For P10 and P11, separate favorable determinations, dollars awarded above baseline, incremental dollars collected, collection lag, and fees actually returned. A prevailing percentage must identify whether its denominator is determinations, cases, or dollars; none is a cash collection rate. Cohort cash realization divides incremental receipts by the corresponding incremental amounts due for the same matured cohort, with reversals handled consistently. Do not compare this week's deposits with this week's awards. Track the thirty-calendar-day payment requirement following the federal determination separately from observed payer behavior. Age unpaid balances from their actual due dates, assign a collection action, and preserve correspondence. A weekly meeting should finish with named corrective owners and dates, not a discussion about who was busiest. Repeated eligibility defects trigger expanded review before more fees are exposed.

Use concentration limits to protect both workload continuity and saleability. Set an internal ceiling of twenty-five percent for any single provider customer and separately for any payer parent group, measured on trailing-twelve-month earned operator revenue. Also inspect incremental receivables and forecast fee exposure because a payer can dominate unpaid awards before dominating collected revenue. Aggregate affiliated practices under their controlling relationship and payer brands under the economically relevant parent; multiple logos do not necessarily diversify risk. A new pod may initially exceed the ceiling. Report that breach explicitly, cap additional discretionary exposure, and pursue other accounts while preserving existing client duties and deadlines. Do not describe a concentrated launch book as diversified. Apply the same discipline to contractor dependency: each critical play must have an operational backup with tested access. Review capacity, concentration, and unresolved defects together each Friday. If new business would consume the deadline reserve, delay onboarding rather than accept volume the pod cannot service. Revenue growth does not justify weak evidence or unexplained fee losses. Retain weekly snapshots so a buyer can distinguish genuine improvement from a dashboard rewritten immediately before diligence. Compare rolling four-week results with the prior period to detect persistent drift rather than overreacting to individual case outcomes.

sop_steps.action: Export the claim ledger, cash matches, deadline queue, and accepted-work register at the agreed cutoff.

sop_steps.action: Inspect every required action due within five business days and confirm its owner, backup, and supporting evidence.

sop_steps.action: Review defects, forfeited fees, overdue awards, and concentration breaches using claim-level records.

sections.heading: 3. Reconcile Cash-Based Fee Waterfalls to Clean Accrual and Cohort Books
paragraphs: Start every engagement with a written recovery waterfall that separates provider money from operator revenue. The initial payer allowed payment is the baseline; the QPA may inform that payment but is not automatically identical to it. Measure incremental cash against the actual documented baseline, including subsequent adjustments without double counting. For an illustrative claim, assume $2,000 initial payment and $8,000 total payer cash ultimately received. Incremental cash is $6,000. If actual non-refundable administrative fees are $150, an entity-fee deposit of $600 is returned following a prevailing determination, and attributable casework costs are $450, the distributable incremental pool is $5,400. At a contracted twenty-five-percent contingency, operator revenue is $1,350, not $8,000 and not the award amount. The example's fees are assumptions, not a current CMS fee schedule. Until the $600 refund actually arrives, an unrecovered-fee waterfall produces a $4,800 pool and $1,200 fee, followed by a $150 true-up after receipt. Losing or ineligible cases retain the applicable forfeited entity-fee exposure. Record actual allocations for settlements and other procedural outcomes separately. Never assume all deposits return or calculate a fee from an uncollected favorable determination.

The canonical Formula v2.0 scenarios remain fixed: Conservative operator revenue of $110,000 less $77,000 expenses yields $33,000 owner profit at thirty percent; Base revenue of $505,000 less $287,850 yields $217,150 at 43.0 percent; Scaled revenue of $900,000 less $396,000 yields $504,000 at fifty-six percent. Conservative and Base use one full-time person plus two contractors; Scaled uses two full-time people plus three contractors. These revenue figures are gross operator fee revenue, not gross medical collections. At the illustrative twenty-five-percent share, the necessary post-cost incremental pools are $440,000, $2,020,000, and $3,600,000 respectively. This sensitivity explains the cases without inventing a universal claim count or collection rate. Amounts deducted before calculating the share must carry explicit funding and reimbursement treatment. If a provider bears casework cost through the waterfall, record that reimbursement or settlement once; do not silently charge the identical cost again against operator profit. Operator-funded unreimbursed casework, contractor overhead, technology, and other operating expenses belong in the stated expense envelope. The $1,800 to $10,500 monthly opex range is not an all-in reconciliation for every scenario; annualized stated expense envelopes exceed that range in Base and Scaled because the full cost bridge must be shown.

Maintain separate dates for service, intake, negotiation, initiation, determination, payer receipt, fee earning, invoicing, and operator collection. The earned contingency condition is incremental payer cash actually collected under the engagement, not merely a favorable award. When that condition and the applicable revenue recognition requirements are satisfied, recognize operator fee revenue and a provider receivable even if the provider pays the invoice later. Keep potential awards and unearned contingent fees in operational schedules rather than booked revenue. Evaluate principal-versus-agent presentation under ASC 606 for reimbursed costs and pass-through funds; do not label provider collections as operator turnover. Separate cash custodial obligations from earned revenue and reconcile any handled client funds by provider. Create cohorts by intake month, provider, payer group, jurisdiction route, and service category. Each cohort should expose submitted volume, eligible volume, fee losses, collected uplift, contractor cost, and time to cash. Accrue incurred contractor work and other expenses in the proper period, estimate collectibility of earned receivables, and record reversals transparently. A buyer should reconcile ledger totals to invoices, payer remittances, and bank records without relying on a founder's spreadsheet explanation. Close monthly with a documented review of unmatched cash and all outstanding entity-fee deposits.

callout.title: Four Checks Before Exposing Fees or Booking a Contingency
callout.body: Use the first three checks before filing and repeat the cash check before recognizing or invoicing the earned recovery share.
items: Verify the applicable federal or state route using service facts, plan funding evidence, and documented exceptions; do not equate every ERISA plan with federal IDR eligibility.
Verify notice delivery, business-day calculations, batch eligibility, relevant cooling-off restrictions, and the operative rule version before committing submission fees.
Verify current administrative and entity charges, losing-case exposure, casework funding, and the signed post-cost contingency waterfall against claim-level expected economics.
Verify incremental payer cash, the original payment baseline, actual fee refunds, attributable costs, and the resulting operator fee before recording earned revenue.

sections.heading: 4. Make the Recovery Book Transferable Before Discussing an Exit Multiple
paragraphs: A transferable book consists of enforceable relationships, reproducible work, clean ownership, and evidence that collections continue without the founder. Provider agreements should address assignment, change of control, termination, access to records, recovery-tail economics, and responsibility for outstanding fees. Obtain required permissions before transferring contracts or sensitive records; a transaction term sheet does not itself authorize disclosure of protected health information. Begin buyer diligence with aggregated cohorts and properly de-identified information where appropriate, then structure necessary access under applicable HIPAA permissions and safeguards. Contractor deliverables need signed intellectual-property assignments under 17 U.S.C. section 204(a) where copyright ownership is transferred. Do not rely solely on a broad work-made-for-hire label for independent contractor software or templates. Identify preexisting contractor tools and secure sufficient transferable licenses for required components. Inventory source code, deadline rules, brief templates, evidence indexes, and operating manuals in a controlled repository. FAIR Health access and other licensed sources require their own usage and transfer review; purchased access does not establish ownership of the underlying material. Keep credentials outside the sale repository. Prove continuity through tested backup access, documented renewals, and a named successor for each of the twelve plays.

Value a normalized earnings stream, not the face amount of pending determinations. For an owner-operated practice, an illustrative two-to-three-times seller discretionary earnings range can serve as a sensitivity, provided the earnings definition, owner compensation, and required owner labor are reconciled. Using Base owner profit of $217,150 as a provisional SDE proxy produces $434,300 to $651,450; it becomes a usable valuation input only after that bridge is verified. These are planning assumptions, not observed transaction comparables. An independently managed operation can instead test a three-to-five-times normalized EBITDA range. If Scaled owner profit of $504,000 excludes a necessary $120,000 replacement manager cost, and no other adjustments apply, the normalized proxy becomes $384,000 and the enterprise-value sensitivity becomes $1,152,000 to $1,920,000. Do not deduct replacement cost twice if it is already inside the $396,000 expense envelope. Owner profit, SDE, and EBITDA are different measures; provide the bridge rather than relabeling them. Determine equity proceeds separately after debt, cash adjustments, working-capital terms, transaction costs, and holdbacks. A higher multiple requires defensible retention, limited concentration, stable cohort collections, and demonstrably transferable execution. A backlog of unpaid awards is not a substitute for those attributes.

Prepare a rolling diligence package even if the intended outcome is a durable cash cow. Include monthly income statements, expense bridges, provider and payer concentration, cohort collection curves, fee-loss history, contractor acceptance records, ownership documents, and the founder-absence test. Separate recurring revenue from one-time catch-up recoveries and expose provider churn rather than blending departed accounts into historical totals. For a sale, define which party owns preclosing awards, postclosing receipts, refunds, and collection costs. If an earnout is used, base it on an auditable measure such as collected operator fees from identified transferred cohorts, with agreed deductions, collection responsibilities, reporting rights, and dispute procedures. An award-based earnout can overpay for balances that never convert to cash. For continued ownership, reserve cash for payroll, contractor commitments, unrecovered fees, and delayed payer remittances before distributions. Stress-test the loss of the largest provider and a prolonged payment delay from the largest payer group. The twenty-five-percent caps limit exposure but do not eliminate it. Choose growth only when it improves normalized cash generation after replacement labor; otherwise preserve the smaller pod. The same disciplined records support either decision without manufacturing a premium narrative around uncertain collections.
